ANNEX B 
( Foreword and Clause 6 ) 
TEST PROCEDURES 


B-1 TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS OF VE- 
HICLE 


B-1.1 Technical specifications of vehicle as relevant to 
brake system shall be declared by the details given in 
Annex A. 


B-1.2 If this information has been declared for type 
approval of the vehicle it is not necessary to submit the 
information again. 


B-2 MODIFICATIONS/CHANGES 


B-2.1 Every functional modification pertaining to 
technical specifications of brake system of vehicle 
declared in accordance with B-1.1 shall be intimated to 
the testing agency. 


B-22 Testing agency may then consider validating 
the test report as per guidelines provided in 
Annex K. 


B-3 CLASSIFICATIONS OF VEHICLES 


B-3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions 
given in AIS 053/ IS 14272 shall be referred. 


B-3.2 Applicability of the Tests 


Based on the applicable Annex the various tests shall 
be conducted on the vehicle submitted for test. 


B-3.2.1 The initial speed shall be the speed at the 
moment when the driver begins to actuate the control 
of the braking system; the initial speed shall not be less 
than 98 percent of the prescribed speed for the test in 
question. 


B-3.2.2 The test shall be carried out at the initial speeds 
prescribed for each type of the test or 90 percent of 
maximum design speed of the vehicle, whichever is 
lower. 


B-3.2.3 During the tests, the force applied to the control 
of the braking system in order to obtain the prescribed 
performance shall not exceed the maximum force 
laid down for the test vehicle's category. Values for 
force measured at speeds below 5 km/h shall not be 
considered. 


B-3.2.4 The road surface shall be dry with a road 
adhesion coefficient of at least 0.8. 


B-4 VISUAL CHECKS 
B-4.1 Check and verify following: 


a) Two independent controls are readily accessible to 
driver from the driver seat while wearing safety 
belt (see 5.2.1.2.1). 


b) It is possible to actuate the service brake control 
even with both hands on steering control even 
while wearing safety belts (see 5.1.2.1). 


с) Service, secondary, and parking brake surfaces 
are permanently connected to the wheels except 
transmission parking brake. 


d) Itis possible to actuate the secondary brake control 
while keeping at least one hand on steering control 
and even while wearing safety belts (see 5.1.2.2). 


e) It shall be possible to lock the parking brake in 
the applied by a purely mechanical device (see 
5.1.2.3). 


f) All brakes shall be provided with automatic 
adjustment for wear. Provision for assessment of 
condition of liner shall be present. Alternatively, 
acoustical or optical devices, warning the driver 
about lining replacement may be fitted (see 
5.2.1.11., 5.2.1.13.1.1) (Optional for N2, N3 off 
road and M1 and NI rear application). 


B-5 INSTRUMENTATION 


B-5.1 Accuracies and least count of the instruments 
shall be as below or better: 


SI No. Parameter Accuracy Least Count 
(1) 0) (3) 4)

ii) a) Pneumatic line pressure + 20 kPa (0.2 bar) 10 kPa (0.1 bar)

iv) | Speed +1 percent of the measured value | 0.1 km/h 
v) Distance + 1 percent of the measured value | 0.1 т

viii) Wind velocity + 0.5 percent of the measured value | 0.5 m/s

B-5.2 Ensure that the instruments/equipment is 
calibrated as per the recommendation of manufacturer 
of instruments/equipment. 


B-5.3 Any other instruments can be used after 
confirmation of satisfactory calibration. 


B-6 TEST TRACK 


B-6.1 Longitudinal and lateral slopes of the track 
shall not exceed 1 percent and 3 percent respectively. 
The track shall have sufficient length and width for 
achieving the test speed and carrying out the test safely. 


B-6.2 If the tests are carried out at the test track of 
the vehicle manufacturer, the conditions specified for 
the test track are deemed to be complied with if the 
manufacturer issues a certificate to that effect. 


B-6.3 For parking brake test, gradient of the track shall 
be constant within + 0.5 percent. 


B-7 VEHICLE PREPARATION 


B-7.1 Before testing the vehicle, ensure that the vehicle 
is run in as per manufacturer's recommendation and 
that the brakes are properly bedded in for brake liner/ 
pad contact. 


B-7.2 Tyres which have covered at least 500 km and 
not more than maximum 10 percent of their expected 
life shall be fitted on the vehicle. These conditions are 
deemed to be complied with if the manufacturer gives a 


written undertaking to that effect. Tyre shall be inflated 
to the pressure specified by vehicle manufacturer for 
respective load condition of the vehicle when the tyres 
are cold. 


B-7.3 Actual weight during testing shall not differ from 
specified laden or unladen weight by: 


a) Unladen : lO percent, Max 
b) Laden : 5 percent, Max 


B-7.4 The distribution of weight among axles shall 
be as specified by the vehicle manufacturer. If sum of 
recommended maximum axle weights exceeds the gross 
vehicle weight, the actual weight on the axle shall be 
in the same proportion of the ratios of the gross vehicle 
weight to the sum of the maximum recommended axle 
weights. Actual load condition shall be recorded in the 
report. 


B-7.5 Weight of the testing personnel and 
instrumentation shall be considered as part of the 
vehicle load and shall be 180 kg in the case of unladen 
test. 


B-7.6 In the case of tractive units for semi-trailers the 
required laden condition shall be achieved by loading 
the tractive unit and not by using a semi-trailer. 


B-7.7 Where the vehicle is not having standard 
production body or is having more than one version 
of standard production body, the following cab/body 
allowance shall apply: 


SI No. Allowance in Weight 
GVW Range Load Body Weight Cab Weight 

kg kg kg 
Q0) Q) (3) (4) 
i) Up to 2 500 120 300 
il) Above 2 500 but below 5 000 200 400 
iii) Above 5 000 but below 7 500 400 500 
iv) Above 7 500 but below 12 000 700 600 
v) Above 12 000 1 000 700 


33 


IS 11852 : 2019 


B-7.8 In the case of incompletely built vehicle (such 
as drive away chassis) suitable arrangements for safety 
of testing personnel during testing shall be provided. 
The weight of such provisions shall be part of the load 
prescribed in B-7.7. 


B-8 SEQUENCE OF TESTING 


B-8.1 All the static tests, the result of, which are 
required in dynamic test, are to be done before the 
dynamic tests. 


B-8.2 There is no preferred sequence during static tests. 


B-8.3 If more than one type of dynamic tests are to 
be carried out, sequence of tests shall be Type 0 test, 
Type I and / or Type II / II-A test. There is no preferred 
sequence among the various Type 0 tests. 


B-8.4 Parking brake test(s) shall be conducted before 
Type I tests. 


B-9 REQUIREMENTS DURING TESTING 


B-9.1 Brake shall not be applied prior to the test within 
800 m immediately before the point at which test 
commences. 


B-9.2 The ambient temperature shall be between 15 to 
45°C. 


B-9.3 The test shall be valid if vehicle does not go out 
of the lane width one and half times the width of the 
vehicle. Wheel locking towards the end of deceleration 
in last three meter shall be permitted. 


B-9.4 In the case of diagonal split secondary brake 
system the force required at the time of steering wheel 


34 


to hold a straight course may be measured and, if felt 
excessive, shall be recorded in the test report. 


B-9.5 Suitable methods for measurement of temperature 
on the disc or outside of the drum may be used. 


NOTE— Measurement of lining/pad temperature is not a 
method for assessing the temperature on the disc or outside of 
the drum. 


B-9.6 Final Result of the Test 


Number of readings to be taken during the test shall be 
as follows: 


a) For all Type 0 tests, maximum six numbers of tests 
shall be carried out; the test need not be carried out 
further once it meets the performance requirement 
during these tests. 


b) All dynamic tests other than Type 0 test shall 
be conducted only once and the result obtained 
during the test shall be the final result. 


c) All static tests other than capacity of the energy 
source shall be conducted only once and the result 
obtained during the test shall be the final result. 


d) Parking brake gradient holding test shall be 
conducted only once. The test shall be conducted 
preferably on the specified gradient. If such a 
gradient is not available, the nearest gradient 
available shall be used. The Gross Vehicle Weight 
(GVW) can be simulated by the following formula. 


G = 100 х tan [sin'((sin Өх W,)/W,)] 
where, 
G = Gradient of vehicle, in percentage; 
— Slope angle of the test track used for the test; 
Wi = Test weight of the vehicle; and 
Wi = Maximum recommended GVW of the vehicle.

ANNEX C 
( Clause 5.1.3.3, 5.1.4.6.3, 5.2.1.4, 5.2.1.7.1, 5.2.1.7.2, 5.2.1.11.1, 5.2.1.18.3, 5.2.1.18.5, 
5.2.2.8.1.1, 5.2.2.8.1.2, 5.2.2.12, 5.2.2.14, 5.2.2.14.1, 5.2.2.14.2, 5.2.2.15.2, 5.2.2.19 and 6 ) 
BRAKING TESTS AND PERFORMANCE OF BRAKING SYSTEMS 


C-1 BRAKING TESTS 
C-1.1 General 


C-1.1.1 The performance prescribed for braking 
systems is based on the stopping distance and/or the 
mean fully developed deceleration. The performance of 
a braking system shall be determined by measuring the 
stopping distance in relation to the initial speed of the 
vehicle and/or by measuring the mean fully developed 
deceleration during the test. 


C-1.1.2 The stopping distance shall be the distance 
covered by the vehicle from the moment when the driver 
begins to actuate the control of the braking system until 
the moment when the vehicle stops; the initial speed 
shall be the speed at the moment when the driver begins 
to actuate the control of the braking system; the initial 
speed shall be within tolerance prescribed in B 3.2.1. 


The mean fully developed deceleration (4) shall be 
calculated as the deceleration averaged with respect 
to distance over the interval v, to v , according to the 
following formula: 


2 
Vb ^ Ve 


— 25.92 (s.-s;) 


2 
52] 


din [m/ 


where, 
v, = vehicle speed at 0.8 у, in km/h; 


v, = vehicle speed at 0.1 у, in km/h; 

v. = initial vehicle speed, in km/h; 

s, = distance travelled between v, and v,, in m; and 
5, = distance travelled between v, and v,, in m. 


The speed and the distance shall be determined using 
instrumentation prescribed in B-5. The mean fully 
developed deceleration may be determined by other 
methods than the measurement of speed and distance; 
in this case, the accuracy of the mean fully developed 
deceleration shall be within +3 percent. 


C-1.2 For the approval of any vehicle, the braking 
performance shall be measured during road tests 
conducted in the following conditions. 


C-1.2.1 The vehicle's condition as regards mass shall 
be as prescribed for each type of test and be specified 
in the test report. 


C-1.2.2 The test shall be carried out at the speeds 
prescribed for each type of test; if the maximum design 


35 


speed of a vehicle is lower than the speed prescribed 
for a test, the test shall be performed at the vehicle's 
maximum speed. 


C-1.2.3 During the tests, the force applied to the control 
of the braking system in order to obtain the prescribed 
performance shall not exceed the maximum force laid 
down for the test vehicle's category. 


C-1.2.4 The road surface shall be dry with a coefficient 
of adhesion as specified in B-3.2.4 


C-1.2.5 The tests shall be performed when there is no 
wind liable to affect the results. 


C-1.2.6 At the start of the tests, the tyres shall be cold 
and at the pressure prescribed as per B-7.2. 


C-1.2.7 The prescribed performance shall be obtained 
without locking of the wheels, without deviation of the 
vehicle from its course and abnormal vibration of the 
vehicle. 


C-1.2.8 For vehicles powered completely or partially by 
an electric motor (or motors), permanently connected 
to the wheels, all tests shall be carried out with the 
motor(s) connected. 


C-1.2.9 For vehicles as described in C-1.2.8, fitted with 
an electric regenerative braking system of category A, 
behaviour tests defined in C-1.4.3.1 shall be carried 
out on a track with a low adhesion coefficient (as 
defined in M-5.2.2). However, the maximum test speed 
shall not exceed the maximum test speed specified in 
M-5.3.1 for a low adhesion surface and the relevant 
vehicle category. 


C-1.2.9.1 Moreover, for vehicles fitted with an electric 
regenerative braking system of category A, transient 
conditions as gear changes or accelerator control 
release shall not affect the behaviour of the vehicle in 
condition of tests described in C-1.2.9. 


C-1.2.10 During the tests specified in C-1.2.9 and 
C-1.2.9.1, wheel locking is not allowed. However, 
steering correction is permitted if the angular rotation 
of the steering control is within 120° during the initial 
2 s and not more than 240° in total. 


C-1.2.11 For a vehicle with electrically actuated 
service brakes powered from traction batteries (or an 
auxiliary battery) which receive(s) energy only from an 


IS 11852 : 2019 


independent external charging system, these batteries 
shall, during braking performance testing, be at an 
average of not more than 5 percent above that state of 
charge at which the brake failure warning prescribed in 
5.2.1.27.6 is required to be given. 


If this warning is given, the batteries may be recharged 
during the tests, to keep them in the required state of 
charge range. 


C-1.3 Behaviour of the Vehicle during Braking 


C-1.3.1 In braking tests, and in particular in those at 
high speed, the general behaviour of the vehicle during 
braking shall be checked. 


C-1.3.2 Behaviour of the Vehicle During Braking on A 
Road on which Adhesion is Reduced 


The behaviour of vehicles of categories M2, M3, N1, 
N2, N3, T3 and T4 on a road on which adhesion is 
reduced, shall meet the relevant requirements of Annex 
J and/or Annex M. 


C-1.3.2.1 In the case of a braking system according to 
5.2.1.7.2, where the braking for a particular axle (or 
axles) is comprised of more than one source of braking 
torque, and any individual source can be varied with 
respect to the other(s), the vehicle shall satisfy the 
requirements of Annex J, or alternatively, Annex M 
under all relationships permitted by its control strategy 
(see Note). 


NOTE— The manufacturer shall provide the Testing Agency 
with the family of braking curves permitted by the automatic 
control strategy employed. These curves may be verified by the 
testing agency. 


C-1.4 Type 0 Test (Ordinary Performance Test with 
Brakes Cold) 


C-1.4.1 General 


C-1.4.1.1 The brakes shall be cold; a brake is deemed 
to be cold when the temperature measured on the disc 
or on the outside of the drum is below 100°C. 


C-1.4.1.2 The test shall be conducted in the following 
conditions: 


C-1.4.1.2.1 The vehicle shall be laden, the distribution 
of its mass among the axles being that stated by the 
manufacturer; where provision is made for several 
arrangements of the load on the axles the distribution 
of the maximum mass among the axles shall be 
such that the load on each axle is proportional to the 
maximum permissible load for each axle. In the case of 
tractors for semi- trailers, the load may be re-positioned 
approximately half-way between the kingpin position 
resulting from the above loading conditions and the 
centre line of the rear axle(s). 


36 


C-1.4.1.2.2 Every test shall be repeated on the unladen 
vehicle. In the case of a power-driven vehicle there 
may be, in addition to the driver, a second person on 
the front seat who is responsible for noting the results 
of the test. 


In the case of a tractor for a semi-trailer, the unladen 
tests will be conducted with the vehicle in its solo 
condition, including a mass representing the fifth 
wheel. It will also include a mass representing a spare 
wheel, if this is included in the standard specification 
of the vehicle. 


In the case of a In completely built vehicle (such as 
Drive Away Chassis) a supplementary load shall be 
added to simulate the mass of the body not exceeding 
the Vehicle kerb weight, declared by the manufacturer 
in Annex A. In absence of this data values specified as 
per B 7.7, shall be used. 


In the case of a vehicle equipped with an electric 
regenerative braking system, the requirements depend 
on the category of this system: 


a) Category A — Any separate electric regenerative 
braking control which is provided, shall not be 
used during the Type 0 tests. 


b) Category B — The contribution of the electric 
regenerative braking system to the braking force 
generated shall not 


exceed that minimum level guaranteed by the system 
design. 


This requirement is deemed to be satisfied if the 
batteries are at one of the following state of charge (see 
Note) conditions where state of charge is determined by 
the method set out in C-5. 
NOTE— By agreement with the Testing Agency, state 
of charge assessment will not be required for vehicles, 
which have an on-board energy source for charging the 
traction batteries and the means for regulating their state 
of charge. 
At the maximum charge level as recommended by 
the manufacturer in the vehicle specification, or at 
a level not less than 95 percent of the full charge 
level, where the manufacturer has made no specific 
recommendation, or at the maximum level which 
results from automatic charge control on the vehicle, 
or when the tests are conducted without a regenerative 
braking component regardless of the state of charge of 
the batteries. 


C-1.4.1.2.3 The limits prescribed for minimum 
performance, both for tests with the vehicle unladen and 
for tests with the vehicle laden, shall be those laid down 
hereunder for each category of vehicles; the vehicle 
shall satisfy both the prescribed stopping distance and/ 
or the prescribed mean fully developed deceleration 
for the relevant vehicle category, but it may not be 
necessary to actually measure both parameters. 


C-1.4.1.2.4 The road shall be level. 


C-1.4.2 Type 0 Test with Engine Disconnected 


The test shall be carried out at the speed prescribed for 
the category to which the vehicle belongs, the Figures 
prescribed in this connection being subject to not less 
than 98 percent of the prescribed speed for the test in 
question. The minimum performance prescribed for 
each category shall be attained. 


C-1.4.3 Type 0 Test with Engine Connected 


C-1.4.3.1 Tests shall also be carried out at various 
speeds, the lowest being equal to 30 percent of the 
maximum speed of the vehicle and the highest being 
equal to 80 percent of that speed. In the case of vehicles 
equipped with a speed limiter, this limiter speed shall 
be taken as the maximum speed of the vehicle. The 
maximum practical performance figures shall be 
measured and the behaviour of the vehicle shall be 
recorded in the test report. Tractors for semi-trailers, 
artificially loaded to simulate the effects of a laden 
semi-trailer shall not be tested beyond 80 km/h. 


C-1.4.3.2 Further tests shall be carried out with the 
engine connected, from the speed prescribed for the 
category to which the vehicle belongs. The minimum 
performance prescribed for each category shall be 
attained. Tractive units for semi-trailers, artificially 
loaded to simulate the effects of a laden semi-trailer 
shall not be tested beyond 80 km/h. 


C-1.4.4 Type 0 Test for Vehicles of Category T, Equipped 
with Compressed Air Brakes 


C-1.4.4.1 The braking performance of the trailer may 
be calculated either from the braking rate of the towing 
vehicle plus the trailer and the measured thrust on the 
coupling or, in certain cases, from the braking rate of 
the towing vehicle plus the trailer with only the trailer 
being braked. The engine of the towing vehicle shall be 
disconnected during the braking test. 


Inthecase whereonly the trailer is braked to take account 
of the extra mass being retarded, the performance will 
be taken to be the mean fully developed deceleration. 


C-1.4.4.2 With the exception of cases according 
to C-1.4.4.3 and C-1.4.4.4, it is necessary for the 
determination of the braking rate of the trailer to 
measure the braking rate of the towing vehicle plus 
the trailer and the thrust on the coupling. The towing 
vehicle has to meet the requirements laid down in 
Annex J with regard to the relationship between the 
ratio T, /P,, and the pressure p . The braking rate of the 
trailer is calculated according to the following formula: 


ZR=ZR+M + —

(compressive force: —D); and 


P, — total normal static reaction between road surface 
and wheels of trailer (see Annex J). 


C-1.4.4.3 If a trailer has a continuous or semi- 
continuous braking system where the pressure in the 
brake actuators does not change during braking despite 
the dynamic axle load shifting and in the case of semi- 
trailers the trailer alone may be braked. The braking rate 
of the trailer is calculated according to the following 
formula:

Annex J). 


C-1.4.4.4 Alternatively, the evaluation of the braking 
rate of the trailer may be done by braking the trailer 
alone. In this case the pressure used shall be the same as 
that measured in the brake actuators during the braking 
of the combination. 


C-1.5 Type I Test (Fade Test) 

C-1.5.1 With Repeated Braking 

C-1.5.1.1 The service braking systems of all power- 
driven vehicles shall be tested by successively applying 


and releasing the brakes a number of times, the vehicle 
being laden, in the conditions shown below: 


Category of Conditions 
Vehicles v, " At Р 
km/h km/h 5

where, 


v, — initial speed, at beginning of braking; 
v, — speed at end of braking; 
v, ^ Maximum speed of vehicle;

IS 11852 : 2019 


At — duration of a braking cycle: time elapsing 
between the initiation of one brake application 
and the initiation of the next. 


C-1.5.1.2 If the characteristics of the vehicle make it 
impossible to abide by the duration prescribed for At, 
the duration may be increased; in any event, in addition 
to the time necessary for braking and accelerating the 
vehicle, a period of 10 s shall be allowed in each cycle 
for stabilizing the speed у. 


C-1.5.1.3 In these tests, the force applied to the control 
shall be so adjusted as to attain the mean fully developed 
deceleration of 3 m/s? at the first brake application; this 
force shall remain constant throughout the succeeding 
brake applications. 


C-1.5.1.4 During brake applications, the highest gear 
ratio (excluding overdrive, etc.) shall be continuously 
engaged. 


C-1.5.1.5 Forregaining speed after braking, the gearbox 
shall be used in such a way as to attain the speed v, 
in the shortest possible time (maximum acceleration 
allowed by the engine and gearbox). 


C-1.5.1.6 For vehicles not having sufficient autonomy 
to carry out the cycles of heating of the brakes, the tests 
shall be carried out by achieving the prescribed speed 
before the first braking application and thereafter by 
using the maximum acceleration available to regain 
speed and then braking successively at the speed reached 
at the end of each time cycle duration as specified, for 
the appropriate vehicle category in C-1.5.1.1. 


C-1.5.1.7 In the case of vehicles equipped with 
automatic brake adjustment devices the adjustment of 
the brakes shall, prior to the Type I test above, be set 
according to the following procedures as appropriate. 


C-1.5.1.7.1 In the case of vehicles equipped with air 
operated brakes the adjustment of the brakes shall be 
such as to enable the automatic brake adjustment device 
to function. For this purpose the actuator stroke shall be 
adjusted to s, 2 1.1 5 „а (the upper limit shall not 
exceed a value recommended by the manufacturer) 


where, 


-— re-adjustment stroke according to the 
specification of the manufacturer of the automatic 
brake adjustment device, that is the stroke, where it 
starts to readjust the running clearance of the brake with 
an actuator pressure of 15 percent of the brake system 
operating pressure but not less than 100 kPa (1 bar). 


Where, by agreement with the certifying agency, it is 
impractical to measure the actuator stroke, the initial 
setting shall be agreed with the certifying agency. 


From the above condition the brake shall be operated 


38 


with an actuator pressure of 30 percent of the brake 
system operating pressure but not less than 200 kPa 
(2 bar), 50 times in succession. This shall be followed 
by a single brake application with an actuator pressure 
of > 650 kPa (6.5 bar). 


C-1.5.1.7.2 In the case of vehicles equipped with 
hydraulically operated disc brakes no setting 
requirements are deemed necessary. 


C-1.5.1.7.3 In the case of vehicles equipped with 
hydraulically operated drum brakes the adjustment of 
the brakes shall be as specified by the manufacturer. 


C-1.5.1.8 For vehicles equipped with an electric 
regenerative braking system of category B, the 
condition of the vehicle batteries at the start of the 
test, shall be such that the braking force contribution 
provided by the electric regenerative braking system 
does not exceed the minimum guaranteed by the 
system design. 


This requirement is deemed to be satisfied if the 
batteries are at one of the state of charge conditions 
listed in C-1.4.1.2.2. 


C-1.5.2 With Continuous Braking 


C-1.5.2.1 The service brakes of trailers of categories T2 
and T3 (when the T3 trailer has not passed alternatively 
the type-II test according to C-1.7) shall be tested in 
such a manner that, the vehicle being laden, the energy 
input to the brakes is equivalent to that recorded in the 
same period of time with a laden vehicle driven at a 
steady speed of 40 km/h on a 7 percent down-gradient 
for a distance of 1.7 km. 


C-1.5.2.2 The test may be carried out on a level road, 
the trailer being drawn by a towing vehicle; during the 
test, the force applied to the control shall be adjusted 
so as to keep the resistance of the trailer constant 
(7 percent of the maximum total stationary axle load 
of the trailer). If the power available for hauling is 
insufficient, the test may be conducted at a lower speed 
but over a greater distance as shown below: 


Speed Distance 
km/h m 


C-1.5.2.3 In the case of trailers equipped with automatic 
brake adjustment devices the adjustment of the brakes 
shall, prior to the Type I test prescribed above, be set 
according to the procedure as laid down in C-1.7.1.1. 


C-1.5.3 Hot Performance 


C-1.5.3.1 At the end of the type I test (test described 
in C-1.5.1 or C-1.5.2) the hot performance of the 
service braking system shall be measured in the same 
conditions (and in particular at a constant control 
force no greater than the mean force actually used) as 
for the Type 0 test with the engine disconnected (the 
temperature conditions may be different). 


C-1.5.3.1.1 For power-driven vehicles the hot 
performance shall not be less than 80 percent of that 
prescribed for the category in question, nor less than 
60 percent of the figure recorded in the Type 0 test with 
the engine disconnected. In calculating the residual 
performance requirements, the percentages are to be 
applied to the second term of polynomial expression of 
stopping distance given in C-2.1.1. 


C-1.5.3.1.2 For vehicles fitted with an electric 
regenerative braking system of category A, during brake 
applications, the highest gear shall be continuously 
engaged and the separate electric regenerative braking 
control, if any, shall not be used. 


C-1.5.3.1.3 In the case of vehicles equipped with an 
electric regenerative braking system of category B, 
having carried out the heating cycles according to 
C-1.5.1.6, the hot performance test shall be carried out 
at the maximum speed which can be reached by the 
vehicle at the end ofthe brake heating cycles, unless the 
speed specified in C-1.4.2 can be reached. 


For comparison, the Type 0 test with cold brakes shall 
be repeated from this same speed and with a similar 
electric regenerative braking contribution, as set by an 
appropriate state of battery charge, as was available 
during the hot performance test. 


Reconditioning of the linings shall be permitted before 
the test is made to compare this second Type 0 cold 
performance with that achieved in the hot test, against 
the criteria of C-1.5.3.1.1 and C-1.5.3.2. 


The tests may be conducted without a regenerative 
braking component. In this case, the requirement on the 
state of charge of the batteries is not applicable. 


C-1.5.3.1.4 However, in the case of trailers, the hot 
brake force at the periphery of the wheels when 
tested at 40 km/h shall not be less than 36 percent of 
the maximum stationary wheel load, nor less than 60 
percent of the figure recorded in the Type 0 test at the 
same speed. 


C-1.5.3.2 In the case of a power-driven vehicle 
which satisfies the 60 percent requirement specified 
in C-1.5.3.1.1, but which cannot comply with the 
80 percent requirement of C-1.5.3.1.1, a further hot 
performance test may be carried out using a control 


39 


IS 11852 : 2019 


force not exceeding that specified in C-2 for the 
relevant vehicle category. The results of both tests shall 
be entered in the report. 


C-1.5.4 Free Running Test 


In the case of motor vehicles equipped with automatic 
brake adjustment devices, the brakes after completing 
the tests defined in C-1.5.3 shall be allowed to cool 
to a temperature representative of a cold brake (that 
is <100°C) and it shall be verified that the vehicle 
is capable of free running by fulfilling one of the 
following conditions: 


a) Wheels are running freely (that is may be rotated 
by hand), and 


b) It is ascertained that when the vehicle is driven at 
a constant speed of v = 60 km/h with the brakes 
released the asymptotic temperatures shall not 
exceed a drum/disc temperature increase of 80 ?C, 
then the residual brake moments are regarded as 
acceptable. 


C-1.6 Type II Test (Downhill Behaviour Test) 


C-1.6.1 Laden power-driven vehicles shall be tested in 
such a manner that the energy input 1s equivalent to 
that recorded in the same period of time with a laden 
vehicle driven at an average speed of 30 km/h on a 6 
percent down-gradient for a distance of 6 km, with the 
appropriate gear engaged and the endurance braking 
(see Note) system such as retarders and exhaust brake 
systems, if the vehicle is equipped with one, being 
used. The gear engaged shall be such that the speed of 
the engine (min!) does not exceed the maximum value 
prescribed by the manufacturer. 


NOTE— Endurance brake means, a supplementary brake 
which is capable of operating for a long duration, without 
or minimum wear on service brake friction material and 
drum. Example engine brake, exhaust brake, hydraulic or 
electromagnetic retarders. These brakes are optional to 
enhance the safety and reduce friction. 


C-1.6.2 For vehicles in which the energy 1s absorbed 
by the braking action of the engine alone, a tolerance 
of + 5 km/h on the average speed shall be permitted, 
and the gear enabling the speed to be stabilized at 
the value closest to 30 km/h on the 6 percent down- 
gradient shall be engaged. If the performance of the 
braking action of the engine alone is determined by a 
measurement of deceleration, it shall be sufficient if the 
mean deceleration measured is at least 0.5 m/s?. 


C-1.6.3 At the end of the test, the hot performance of 
the service braking system shall be measured in the 
same conditions as for the Type 0 test with the engine 
disconnected (the temperature conditions may be 
different). This hot performance shall give a stopping 
distance not exceeding the following values and a mean 
fully developed deceleration not less than the following 


IS 11852 : 2019 


values, using a control force not exceeding 70 daN (kg): 


a) Category M3 0.15v + (1.33 v?/130) (the second 
term corresponds to a mean fully developed 
deceleration d = 3.75 m/s’); and 


b) Category N3 0.15v + (1.33 v’/115)(the second 
term corresponds to a mean fully developed 
deceleration d = 3.3 m/s”). 


C-1.6.4 Vehicles cited in C-1.8.1.1, C-1.8.1.2 and 
C-1.8.1.3 shall satisfy the Type IIA test described in 
C-1.8 instead of the Type II test. 


C-1.7 Type III Test (Fade Test for Vehicles of Cate- 
gory T4 or Alternatively of Category T3) 


C-1.7.1 Track Test 


C-1.7.1.1 The adjustment of the brakes shall, prior to 
the Type III test below, be set according to the following 
procedures as appropriate: 


C-1.7.1.1.1 In the case of trailers equipped 
with air operated brakes the adjustment of the 
brakes shall be such as to enable the automatic 
brake adjustment device to function. For this 
purpose the actuator stroke shall be adjusted to 
502 1.1 s, (the upper limit shall not exceed a value 
recommended by the manufacturer) 


Where, 


Bosw is the re-adjustment stroke according to the 
specification of the manufacturer of the automatic 
brake adjustment device, that is the stroke, where 
it starts to re-adjust the running clearance of the 


brake with an actuator pressure of 100 kPa (1 bar). 


Where, by agreement with the Certifying Agency, it is 
impractical to measure the actuator stroke, the initial 
setting shall be agreed with the Certifying Agency. 


From the above condition the brake shall be operated 
with an actuator pressure of 200 kPa (2 bar), 50 times 
in succession. This shall be followed by a single brake 
application with an actuator pressure of > 650 kPa 
(6.5 bar). 


C-1.7.1.1.2 In the case of trailers equipped with 
hydraulically operated disc brakes no setting 
requirements are deemed necessary. 


C-1.7.1.1.3 In the case of trailers equipped with 
hydraulically operated drum brakes the adjustment of 
the brakes shall be as specified by the manufacturer. 


C-1.7.1.2 For the road test the conditions shall be as 
follows:

C-1.7.2 Hot Performance 


At the end of the test according to C-1.7.1, the hot 
performance of the service braking system shall be 
measured under the same conditions as for the Type 
0 test with, however, different temperature conditions 
and starting from an initial speed of 60 km/h. The hot 
brake-force at the periphery of the wheels shall then 
not be less than 40 percent of the maximum stationary 
wheel load, and not less than 60 percent of the figure 
recorded in the Type 0 test at the same speed. 


C-1.7.3 Free Running Test 


After completing the tests defined in C-1.7.2, the brakes 
shall be allowed to cool to a temperature representative 
of a cold brake (that is < 100°C) and it shall be verified 


that the trailer is capable of free running by fulfilling 
one of the following conditions: 


a) Wheels are running freely (that is, may be rotated 
by hand); and 

b) It is ascertained that when the trailer is driven at a 
constant speed of v = 60 km/h with the brakes released 
the asymptotic temperatures shall not exceed a drum/ 
disc temperature increase of 80 ?C, then the residual 
brake moments are regarded as acceptable. 


C-1.8 Type IIA Test (Endurance Braking Perfor- 
mance) 


C-1.8.1 Vehicles of the following categories shall be 
subject to the Type-IIA test: 


C-1.8.1.1 Interurban motor coaches and long distance 
touring motor coaches of category M3. 


C-1.8.1.2 Vehicles of category N3 which are authorized 
to tow a trailer of category T4 


Ifthe maximum mass exceeds 26 t, the test mass is limited 
to 26 t or, in the case where the unladen mass exceeds 
26 t, this mass is to be taken into account by calculation. 


C-1.8.1.3 Certain vehicles subject to ADR (Annex D) 


NOTE— Mandatory compliance to Type IIA Test will be in 
accordance with decision of statutory authority. 


C-1.8.2 Test Conditions and Performance Require- 
ments 


C-1.8.2.1 The performance of the endurance braking 
system shall be tested at the maximum mass of the 
vehicle or of the vehicle combination. 


IS 11852 : 2019 


C-1.8.2.2 Laden vehicles shall be tested in such a 
manner that the energy input is equivalent to that 
recorded in the same period of time with a laden 
vehicle driven at an average speed of 30 km/h on a 
7 percent down-gradient for a distance of 6 km. During 
the test, the service, secondary and parking braking 
systems shall not be engaged. The gear engaged shall 
be such that the speed of the engine does not exceed 
the maximum value prescribed by the manufacturer. 
An integrated endurance braking system may be used, 
provided that it is suitably phased such that the service 
braking system is not applied; this may be verified 
by checking that its brakes remain cold, as defined in 
C-1.4.1.1. 


C-1.8.2.3 For vehicles in which the energy is absorbed 
by the braking action of the engine alone, a tolerance 
of +5 km/h on the average speed shall be permitted, 
and the gear enabling the speed to be stabilized at a 
value closest to 30 km/h on a 7 percent down-gradient 
shall be engaged. If the performance of the braking 
action of the engine alone is determined by measuring 
the deceleration, it shall be sufficient if the mean 
deceleration measured is at least 0.6 m/s?. 


C-2 PERFORMANCE OF BRAKING SYSTEMS 
OF VEHICLES OF CATEGORIES M2, M3 AND N

C-2.2 Secondary Braking System 


C-2.2.1 The secondary braking system, even if the 
control which actuates it is also used for other braking 
functions, shall give a stopping distance not exceeding 
the following values and a mean fully developed 
deceleration not less than the following values: 


a) Category M2, МЗ 0.15 v + (212/130) (the 
second term corresponds to a mean fully developed 
deceleration d, = 2.5 m/s?) 


b) Category М 0.15 v + (2v’/115) (the second 
term corresponds to a mean fully developed 
deceleration d = 2.2 m/s?) 


C-2.2.2 If the control is hand control, the prescribed 
performance shall be obtained by applying to the 
control a force not exceeding 60 daN (kg) in the case of 
other vehicles, and the control shall be so placed that it 
can be easily and quickly grasped by the driver. 


C-2.2.3 If itis a foot control, the prescribed performance 
shall be obtained by applying to the control a force not 
exceeding 70 daN (kg) in the case of other vehicles, and 
the control shall be so placed that it can be easily and 
quickly actuated by the driver. 


42 


C-2.2.4 The performance of the secondary braking 
system shall be checked by the Type 0 test with engine 
disconnected from the following initial speeds: 


a) M2: 60 km/h M3: 60 km/h 
b) NI: 70 km/h N2: 50 km/h N3: 40 km/h 


C-2.2.5 The secondary braking effectiveness test shall 
be conducted by simulating the actual failure conditions 
in the service braking system. 


C-2.2.6 For vehicles employing electric regenerative 
braking systems, the braking performance shall 
additionally be checked under the two following failure 
conditions. 


C-2.2.6.1 For a total failure of the electric component 
of the service braking output. 


C-2.2.6.2 In the case where the failure condition causes 
the electric component to deliver its maximum braking 
force. 


C-2.3 Parking Braking System 


C-2.3.1 The parking braking system shall, even if it 
is combined with one of the other braking systems, be 
capable of holding the laden vehicle stationary on an 18 
percent up or down-gradient. 


C-2.3.2 On vehicles to which the coupling of a trailer 
is authorized, the parking braking system of the towing 
vehicle shall be capable of holding the combination of 
vehicles stationary on a 12 percent up or down-gradient. 


C-2.3.3 If the control is manual, the force applied to 
it shall not exceed 60 daN (kg) in the case of all other 
vehicles. 


C-2.3.4 If it is a foot control, the force exerted on the 
control shall not exceed 70 daN (kg) in the case of all 
other vehicles. 


C-2.3.5 A parking braking system which has to be 
actuated several times before it attains the prescribed 
performance is admissible. 


C-2.3.6 To check compliance with the requirement 
specified in 5.2.1.2.4, a Type 0 test shall be carried out 
with the engine disconnected at an initial test speed of 
30 km/h. The mean fully developed deceleration on 
application of the control of the parking brake system 
and the deceleration immediately before the vehicle 
stops shall not be less than 1.5 m/s?. The test shall be 
carried out with the laden vehicle. 


The force exerted on the braking control device shall 
not exceed the specified values. 


C-2.4 Residual Braking After Transmission Failure 


C-2.4.1 The residual performance of the service 
braking system, in the event of failure in a part of 
its transmission, shall give a stopping distance not 
exceeding the following values and a mean fully 
developed deceleration not less than the following 
values, using a control force not exceeding 70 daN 
(kg), when checked by the Type 0 test with the engine 
disconnected from the following initial speeds for the 
relevant vehicle category: 


C-2.4.2 The residual braking effectiveness test shall be 
conducted by simulating the actual failure conditions in 
the service braking system. 


C-3 PERFORMANCE OF BRAKING SYSTEMS 
OF VEHICLES OF CATEGORY T 


C-3.1 Service Braking System 


C-3.1.1 Provision Relating to Tests of Vehicles of Cat- 
egory Т1 


Where the provision of a service braking system is 
mandatory, the performance of the system shall meet 
the requirements laid down for vehicles of categories 
T2 and T3. 


C-3.1.2 Provisions Relating to Tests of Vehicles of Cat- 
egories T2 and T3 


C-3.1.2.1 If the service braking system is of the 
continuous or semi-continuous type, the sum of the 
forces exerted on the periphery of the braked wheels 
shall be at least x percent of the maximum stationary 
wheel load, x having the following values: 


x [percent]

C-3.1.2.2 If the trailer is fitted with a compressed-air 
braking system, the pressure in the supply line shall 
not exceed 700 kPa (7 bar) during the brake test and 
the signal value in the control line shall not exceed the 
following values, depending on the installation: 


a) 650 kPa (6.5 bar) in the pneumatic control line; 
and 


b) A digital demand value corresponding to 650 kPa 
(6.5 bar) as defined in ISO 11992 and ISO 11992- 
2 its Amd 1 in the electric control line.

comparison with the Type I test result. 


C-3.1.2.3 If the braking system is of the inertia type, it 
shall comply with the requirements of Annex L. 


C-3.1.2.4 In addition, the vehicles shall undergo the 
Type I test or alternatively a Type III test in the case of 
T3 Trailer. 


C-3.1.2.5 In the Type I or the Type III test of a semi- 
trailer, the mass braked by the latter's axle(s) shall 
correspond to the maximum axle load(s) (not including 
the king pin load).

C-3.1.3.2 If the trailer is fitted with a compressed air

line shall not exceed 700 kPa (7 bar) during the brake

C-3.1.3.3 In addition, the vehicles shall undergo the

C-3.1.3.4 In the Type III test of a semi-trailer, the mass 
braked by the latter's axle(s) shall correspond to the 
maximum axle load(s). 


C-3.2 Parking Braking System 


C-3.2.1 The parking braking system with which the 
trailer is equipped shall be capable of holding the laden 
traller stationary, when separated from the towing 
vehicle, on an 18 percent up or down-gradient. The 
force applied to the control device shall not exceed 
60 daN (kg). 


C-3.3 Automatic Braking System 


C-3.3.1 The automatic braking performance in the 
event of a failure, as described in 5.2.1.18.3, when 
testing the laden vehicle from a speed of 40 km/h, shall 
not be less than 13.5 percent of the maximum stationary 
wheel load. Wheel-locking at performance levels above 
13.5 percent is permitted. 


C-4 RESPONSE TIME 


C-4.1 Where a vehicle is equipped with a service 
braking system which is totally or partially dependent 
on a source of energy other than the muscular effort of 
the driver, the following requirements shall be satisfied. 


C-4.1.1 In an emergency manoeuvre, the time elapsing 
between the moment when the control device begins 
to be actuated and the moment when the braking force 
on the least favourably placed axle reaches the level 
corresponding to the prescribed performance shall not 
exceed 0.6 s. 


C-4.1.2 In the case of vehicles fitted with compressed- 
air braking systems, the requirements of C-4.1.1 are 


44 


considered to be satisfied if the vehicle complies with 
the provisions of Annex E. 


C-4.1.3 In the case of vehicles fitted with hydraulic 
braking systems, the requirements of C-4.1.1 
are considered to be satisfied if in an emergency 
manoeuvre, the deceleration of the vehicle or the 
pressure at the least favourable brake cylinder, reaches 
a level corresponding to the prescribed performance 
within 0.6 s. 


C-5 PROCEDURE FOR MONITORING THE 
STATE OF BATTERY CHARGE 


This procedure is applicable to vehicle batteries used 
for traction and regenerative braking. The procedure 
requires the use of a bi-directional dc watt-hour meter. 


C-5.1 Procedure 


C-5.1.1 If the batteries are new or have been subject to 
extended storage, they shall be cycled as recommended 
by the manufacturer. A minimum 8 h soak period at 
ambient temperature shall be allowed after completion 
of cycling. 


C-5.1.2 A full charge shall be established using the 
manufacturer's recommended charging procedure. 


C-5.1.3 When the braking tests of C-1.2.11, C-1.4.1.2.2, 
C-1.5.1.6, and C-1.5.3.1.3 are conducted the watt- 
hours consumed by the traction motors and supplied by 
the regenerative braking system shall be recorded as a 
running total which shall then be used to determine the 
state of charge existing at the beginning or end of a 
particular test. 


C-5.1.4 To replicate a level of state of charge in the 
batteries for comparative tests, such as those of 
C-1.5.3.1.3, the batteries shall be either recharged to 
that level or charged to above that level and discharged 
into a fixed load at approximately constant power until 
the required state of charge is reached. Alternatively, for 
vehicles with battery powered electric traction only, the 
state of charge may be adjusted by running the vehicle. 
Tests conducted with a battery partially charged at their 
start shall be commenced as soon as possible after the 
desired state of charge has been reached. 


IS 11852 : 2019 


ANNEX D 
( Clause 6 and C-1.8.1.3 ) 


ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS APPLICABLE TO CERTAIN VEHICLES 
MEANT FOR CARRIAGE OF DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS GOODS 


D-1 SCOPE 


This Annex applies to certain vehicles meant for the 
carriage of dangerous and hazardous goods vehicles 
with respect to specific requirements concerning anti- 
lock and endurance braking performance. 


D-2 REQUIREMENTS 


D-2.1 General Provisions 


Power-driven vehicles and trailers intended for use 
as transport units for dangerous goods shall fulfil all 
relevant technical requirements of this standard. In 
addition, the following technical provisions shall apply 
as appropriate. 


D-2.2 Anti-Lock Braking System of Trailers 


Trailers of category T4 shall be equipped with 
category 1 anti-lock systems as defined in Annex M. 


D-2.3 Endurance Braking System 


D-2.3.1 Power-driven vehicles having a maximum 
mass exceeding 16 t, or authorized to tow a trailer of 
category T4 shall be fitted with an endurance braking 
system according to 3.15 which complies with the 
following requirements: 


a) The endurance braking control configurations 
shall be from a type described in 3.15.2.1 to 
3.15.2.3; 


b) In the case of an electrical failure of the anti- 
lock system, integrated or combined endurance 
braking systems shall be switched off 
automatically; 


45 


c) The effectiveness of the endurance braking system 
shall be controlled by the anti-lock braking system 
such that the axle(s) braked by the endurance 
braking system cannot be locked by that system at 
speeds above 15 km/h. However, this requirement 
shall not apply to that part of the braking system 
constituted by the natural engine braking; 

d) The endurance braking system shall comprise 

several stages of effectiveness, including a low 

stage appropriate for the unladen condition. 

Where the endurance braking system of a power- 

driven vehicle is constituted by its engine, the 

different gear ratios shall be considered to provide 
the different stages of effectiveness; and 

е) The performance of the endurance braking system 

shall be such that it fulfils the requirements of 

C-1.8 (Type IIA test), with a laden vehicle mass 

comprising the laden mass of the motor vehicle 

and its authorized maximum towed mass but not 

exceeding a total of 44 t. 


D-2.3.2 If a trailer 1s equipped with an endurance 
braking system it shall fulfil the requirements of 
D-2.3.1 (a to d) as appropriate. 


D-2.4. Braking requirements for EX/III vehicles of 
categories T1 and T2 


D-2.4.1 Not withstanding the provisions of paragraph 
5.2.2.9 of this Regulation, EX/III vehicles, as defined 
in Regulation No. 105, of categories Т1 and T2, 
irrespective of their mass, shall be equipped with a 
braking system which automatically brakes the trailer 
to a stop if the coupling device separates while the 
trailer is in motion. 


IS 11852 : 2019 


ANNEX E 
( Clauses 5.1.4.2 and C-4.1.2 ) 


METHOD OF MEASURING THE RESPONSE TIME ON VEHICLES 
EQUIPPED WITH COMPRESSED AIR BRAKING SYSTEMS 


E-1 GENERAL 


E-1.1 The response times of the service braking 
system shall be determined on the stationary vehicle, 
the pressure being measured at the intake to the 
cylinder of the least favourably placed brake. In the 
case of vehicles fitted with combined compressed 
air/hydraulic braking systems, the pressure may 
be measured at the opening of the least favourably 
placed pneumatic unit. For vehicles equipped with 
load sensing valves, these devices shall be set in the 
‘laden’ position. 


E-1.2 During the test, the stroke of the brake cylinders 
of the various axles shall be that required for brakes 
adjusted as closely as possible. 


E-1.3 The response times determined in accordance 
with the provisions of this Annex shall be rounded to 
the nearest tenth of a second. If the figure representing 
the hundredth is five or more, the response time shall be 
rounded up to the next higher tenth. 


E-2 POWER DRIVEN VEHICLES 


E-2.1 At the beginning of each test, the pressure in the 
energy storage device shall be equal to the pressure at 
which the governor restores the feed to the system. In 
systems not equipped with a governor (for example, 
pressure-limited compressors) the pressure in the 
energy storage device at the beginning of each test 
shall be 90 percent of the pressure specified by the 
manufacturer and defined in F-1.2.2.1, used for the 
tests prescribed in this Annex. 


E-2.2 The response times as a function of the 
actuating time (¢,) shall be obtained by a succession 
of full actuations, beginning with the shortest 
possible actuating time and increasing to a time of 
about 0.4 s. The measured values shall be plotted on 
a graph. 


E-2.3 The response time to be taken into consideration 
for the purpose of the test is that corresponding to 
an actuating time of 0.2 s. This response time can be 
obtained from the graph by interpolation. 


E-2.4 For an actuating time of 0.2 s, the time elapsing 
from the initiation of the braking system control 
actuation to the moment when the pressure in the brake 
cylinder reaches 75 percent of its asymptotic value 
shall not exceed 0.6 s. 


46 


E-2.5 In the case of power-driven vehicles having 
a pneumatic control line for trailers, in addition to 
the requirements of E 1.1.the response time shall be 
measured at the extremity of a pipe 2.5 m long with an 
internal diameter of 13 mm which shall be joined to the 
coupling head of the control line of the service braking 
system. During this test, a volume of 385 cm? € 5 cm? 
(which is deemed to be equivalent to the volume of a 
pipe 2.5 m long with an internal diameter of 13 mm and 
under a pressure of 650 kPa) shall be connected to the 
coupling head of the supply line. 


Tractors for semi-trailers shall be equipped with flexible 
pipes for making the connection to semi-trailers. The 
coupling heads will, therefore, be at the extremity of 
those flexible pipes. The length and internal diameter 
of the pipes shall be recorded in test report. 


In the case of an automated connector the measurement 
including the use of a 2.5 m pipe and 385 cm? 5 cm? of 
volume as described above shall be made, considering 
the connector interface as the coupling heads." 


E-2.6 The time elapsing from the initiation of brake 
pedal actuation to the moment when 


a) the pressure measured at the coupling head of the 
pneumatic control line; and 


b) the digital demand value in the electric control 
line measured according to ISO 11992 : 2003 
including ISO 11992-2 and its Amendment 1 
reaches x percent of its asymptotic, respectively 
final value shall not exceed the times shown in the 


table below: 
X t 
percent S 
10 0.2 
75 0.4 


E-2.7 In the case of power-driven vehicles authorized to 
tow trailers ofcategory T3 or T4 fitted with compressed- 
air braking systems, in addition to the above mentioned 
requirements, the prescriptions in 5.2.1.18.4.1 shall be 
verified by conducting the following test: 


a) By measuring the pressure at the extremity of 
a pipe 2.5 m long with an internal diameter of 
13 mm which shall be joined to the coupling head 
of the supply line, 


b) By simulating a failure of the control line at the 
coupling head, and 


c) By actuating the service braking control device in 
0.2 s, as described in F-2.3. 


E-3 TRAILERS 


E-3.1 The trailer's response times shall be measured 
without the power-driven vehicle. To replace the 
power-driven vehicle, it is necessary to provide a 
simulator to which the coupling heads of the supply 
line, the pneumatic control line and/or the connector of 
the electric control line are connected. 


E-3.2 The pressure in the supply line shall be 650 kPa 
(6.5 bar). 


E-3.3 The simulator for pneumatic control lines shall 
have the following characteristics: 


a) It shall have a reservoir with a capacity of 30 
litre which shall be charged to a pressure of 650 
kPa (6.5 bar) before each test and which shall 
not be recharged during each test. At the outlet 
of the braking control device, the simulator shall 
incorporate an orifice with a diameter of from 
4.0 to 4.3 mm inclusive. The volume of the pipe 
measured from the orifice up to and including 
the coupling head shall be 385 + 5 cm? [which is 
deemed to be equivalent to the volume of a pipe 
2.5 m long with an internal diameter of 13 mm 
and under a pressure of 650 kPa (6.5 bar)]. The 
control line pressures referred to in F-3.3.3 shall be 
measured immediately downstream of the orifice. 


b 


wm 


The braking system control shall be so designed 
that its performance in use is not affected by the 
tester. 


С 


ме 


The simulator shall be set, for example, through 
the choice of orifice in accordance with E - 3.3.(a) 
in such a way that, if a reservoir of 385 cm3 + 5 
cm? is joined to it, the time taken for the pressure 
to increase from 65 to 490 kPa (10 and 75 per cent 
respectively of the nominal pressure of 650 kPa) 
shall be 0.2 second + 0.01 second. If a reservoir of 
1,155 cm? + 15 cm? is substituted for the above- 
mentioned reservoir, the time taken for the pressure 
to increase from 65 to 490 kPa without further 
adjustment shall be 0.38 s + 0.02 s. Between these 
two pressure values, the pressure shall increase 
in an approximately linear way. These reservoirs 
shall be connected to the coupling head without 
using flexible pipes. The connection between the 
reservoirs and the coupling head shall have an 
internal diameter of not less than 10 mm. The 
setting shall be carried out using a coupling head 
arrangement that is representative of the type fitted 
to the trailer for which type approval is sought. 


d 


М7 


Figure 3 to 5 (see E-4) give ап example of ће 
correct configuration of the simulator for setting 
and use. 

E-3.4 The simulator for checking the response to 
signals transmitted via the electric control line shall 
have the following characteristics: 


47 


IS 11852 : 2019 


a) The simulator shall produce a digital demand 
signal in the electric control line according to 
ISO 11992-2 and its Amd.1 and shall provide 
the appropriate information to the trailer via 
pins 6 and 7 of the ISO 7638 : 2003 (Part 1 
or 2) connector. For the purpose of response 
time measurement the simulator may at the 
manufacturer's request transmit to the trailer 
information that no pneumatic control line is 
present and that the electric control line demand 
signal is generated from two independent circuits 
(see 6.4.2.2.24 and 6.4.2.2.25 of ISO 11992-2 and 
its Amd.1). 

The braking system control shall be so designed 
that its performance in use is not affected by the 
tester. 


b) 


С 


— 


For the purpose of response time measurement the 
signal produced by the electric simulator shall be 
equivalent to a linear pneumatic pressure increase 
from 0 to 650 kPa in 0.2 + 0.01 s. 

The diagrams in E-4 give an example of the 
correct configuration of the simulator for setting 
and use. 


d) 


E-3.5 Performance Requirements 


E-3.5.1 For trailers with a pneumatic control line the 
time elapsing between the moments when the pressure 
produced in the control line by the simulator reaches 
650 kPa and the moment when the pressure in the 
brake actuator of the trailer reaches 75 percent of its 
asymptotic value shall not exceed 0.4 s. 


E-3.5.1.1Trailers equipped with a pneumatic control 
line and having electric control transmission shall be 
checked with the electrical power supplied to the trailer 
via ISO 7638 connector (5 or 7 pin). 


E-3.5.2 For trailers with an electric control line the 
time elapsing between the moment when the signal 
produced by the simulator exceeds the equivalent of 65 
kPa (0.65 bar) and the moment when the pressure in 
the brake actuator of the trailer reaches 75 percent of its 
asymptotic value shall not exceed 0.4 s. 


E-3.5.3 In the case of trailers equipped with a 
pneumatic and an electric control line, the response 
time measurement for each control line shall be 
determined independently according to the relevant 
procedure defined above.

( Clauses 5.1.4.2, 5.2.1.5.2, 5.2.1.5.3, 5.2.1.13.1.1, 5.2.1.27.5, 5.2.1.27.6,

PROVISIONS RELATING TO ENERGY SOURCES AND ENERGY STORAGE 
DEVICES (ENERGY ACCUMULATORS) 


SECTION A COMPRESSED AIR BRAKING SYSTEMS 


F-1 CAPACITY OF ENERGY STORAGE DE- 
VICES (ENERGY RESERVOIRS) 


F-1.1 General 


F-1.1.1 Vehicles on which the operation of the 
braking system requires the use of compressed-air 
shall be equipped with energy storage devices (energy 
accumulators) of a capacity meeting the requirements 
of F-1.2 and F- 1.3. 


F-1.1.2 It shall be possible to easily identify the 
reservoirs of the different circuits. 


F-1.1.3 However, the energy storage devices shall not 
be required to be of a prescribed capacity if the braking 
system is such that in the absence of any energy reserve 
it is possible to achieve a braking performance at least 
equal to that prescribed for the secondary braking 
system. 


F-1.1.4 In verifying compliance with the requirements 
of F-1.2 and F-1.3, the brakes shall be adjusted as 
closely as possible. 


F-1.2 Power-Driven Vehicles 


F-1.2.1 The energy storage devices (energy reservoirs) 
of power-driven vehicles shall be such that after eight 
full-stroke actuations of the service braking system 
control the pressure remaining in the energy storage 
device(s) shall be not less than the pressure required 
to obtain the specified secondary braking performance. 


F-1.2.2 Testing shall be performed in conformity with 
the following requirements. 


F-1.2.2.1 The initial energy level in the energy storage 
device(s) shall be that specified by the manufacturer. It 
shall be such as to enable the prescribed performance of 
the service braking system to be achieved. 


NOTE— The initial energy level shall be stated in the approval 
document. 


F-1.2.2.2 The energy storage device(s) shall not be fed; 
in addition, any energy storage device(s) for auxiliary 
equipment shall be isolated. 


F-1.2.2.3 In the case of power-driven vehicle to which 
the coupling of a trailer is authorized and with a 


50 


pneumatic control line, the supply line shall be stopped 
and a compressed-air reservoir of 0.5 1 capacity shall 
be connected directly to the coupling head of the 
pneumatic control line. Before each braking operation, 
the pressure in this compressed-air reservoir shall be 
completely eliminated. After the test referred to in 
F-1.2.1 the energy level supplied to the pneumatic 
control line shall not fall below a level equivalent to one- 
half the Figure obtained at the first brake application. 


F-1.3 Trailers 


F-1.3.1 The energy storage devices (energy reservoirs) 
with which trailers are equipped shall be such that, 
after eight full-stroke actuations of the towing vehicle's 
service braking system, the energy level supplied to the 
operating members using the energy does not fall below 
a level equivalent to one-half of the figure obtained at 
the first brake application and without actuating either 
the automatic or the parking braking system of the 
trailer. 


F-1.3.2 Testing shall be performed in conformity with 
the following requirements: 


a) The pressure in the energy storage devices at the 
beginning of each test shall be 850 kPa (8.5 bar); 


b) The supply line shall be stopped; in addition, any 
energy storage device(s) for auxiliary equipment 
shall be isolated; 


c) Theenergy storage devices shall not be replenished 
during the test; 


d) At each brake application, the pressure in the 
pneumatic control line shall be 750 kPa (7.5 bar); 
and 


e) Ateach brake application, the digital demand value 
in the electric control line shall be corresponding 
to a pressure of 750 kPa (7.5 bar). 


F-2 CAPACITY OF ENERGY SOURCES 


F-2.1 General 


The compressors shall meet the requirements set forth 
in the following paragraphs. 


F-2.2 Definitions 


F-2.2.1 ‘p,’ is the pressure corresponding to 65 percent 
of the pressure ‘p,’ defined in F-2.2.2. 


Е-2.2.2 ‘p,’ is the value specified by the manufacturer 
and referred to in F-1.2.2.1. 


Е-2.2.3 “1° is the time required for the relative pressure 
to rise from 0 to p,, and ‘T, is the time required for the 
relative pressure to rise from 0 to p,. 


F-2.3 Conditions of Measurement 


F-2.3.1 In all cases, the speed of the compressor shall 
be that obtained when the engine is running at the speed 
corresponding to its maximum power or at the speed 
allowed by the governor. 


F-2.3.2 During the tests to determine the time t, and 
the time t,, the energy storage device(s) for auxiliary 
equipment shall be isolated. 


F-2.3.3 If it is intended to attach a trailer to a power- 
driven vehicle, the trailer shall be represented by 
an energy storage device whose maximum relative 
pressure p (expressed in kPa / 100) is that which can 
be supplied through the towing vehicle’s supply circuit 
and whose volume V, expressed in litres, is given by the 
formula p x V= 20 R (R being the permissible maximum 
mass, in tonnes, on the axles of the trailer). 


F-2.4 Interpretation of Results 


Е-2.4.1 The time ¢, recorded for the least favoured 
energy storage device shall not exceed: 


F-2.4.1.1 Three minutes in the case of vehicles to which 
the coupling of a trailer is not authorized; or 


F-2.4.1.2 Six minutes in the case of vehicles to which 
the coupling of a trailer is authorized. 


Е-2.4.2 The time f, recorded for the least favoured 
energy storage device shall not exceed: 


F-2.4.2.1 Six minutes in the case of vehicles to which 
the coupling of a trailer is not authorized; or 


F-2.4.2.2 Nine minutes in the case of vehicles to which 
the coupling of a trailer is authorized. 


F-2.5 Additional Test 


F-2.5.1 Ifthe power-driven vehicle is equipped with one 
or more energy storage devices for auxiliary equipment 
having a total capacity exceeding 20 percent of the 
total capacity of the braking energy storage devices, 
an additional test shall be performed during which no 
irregularity shall occur in the operation of the valves 
controlling the filling of the energy storage device(s) 
for auxiliary equipment. 


51 


IS 11852 : 2019 


F-2.5.2 It shall be verified during the aforesaid test that 
the time /, necessary to raise the pressure from 0 to p, 
in the least favoured braking energy storage device is 
less than. 


F-2.5.2.1 Eight minutes in the case of vehicles to which 
the coupling of a trailer is not authorized; or 


F-2.5.2.2 Eleven minutes in the case of vehicles to 
which the coupling of a trailer is authorized. 


F-2.5.3 The test shall be performed in the conditions 
prescribed in F-2.3.1 and F-2.3.3. 


F-2.6 Towing Vehicles 


F-2.6.1 Power driven vehicles to which the coupling 
of a trailer is authorized shall also comply with the 
above requirements for vehicles not so authorized. In 
that case, the tests in F-2.4.1 and F-2.4.2 (and F-2.5.2) 
shall be conducted without the energy storage device 
mentioned in F-2.3.3. 


SECTION B VACUUM BRAKING SYSTEMS 


F-3 CAPACITY OF ENERGY STORAGE DE- 
VICES (ENERGY RESERVOIRS) 


F-3.1 General 


F-3.1.1 Vehicles on which operation of the braking 
system requires the use of a vacuum shall be equipped 
with energy storage devices (energy reservoirs) of a 
capacity meeting the requirements of F-3.2 and F-3.3. 


F-3.1.2 However, the energy storage devices shall not 
be required to be of a prescribed capacity if the braking 
system is such that in the absence of any energy reserve 
it is possible to achieve a braking performance at least 
equal to that prescribed for the secondary braking system. 


F-3.1.3 In verifying compliance with the requirements 
of F-3.2 and F-3.3, the brakes shall be adjusted as 
closely as possible. 


F-3.2 Power Driven Vehicles 


F-3.2.1 The energy storage devices (energy reservoirs) 
of power-driven vehicles shall be such that it is still 
possible to achieve the performance prescribed for the 
secondary braking system: 


a) After eight full stroke actuations of the service 
braking system control where the energy source is 
a vacuum pump; and 


b) After four full stroke actuations of the service 
brake control where the energy source is the 
engine. 


IS 11852 : 2019 


F-3.2.2 Testing shall be performed in conformity with 
the following requirements: 


a) The initial energy level in the energy storage 
device(s) shall be that specified by the 
manufacturer. It shall be such as to enable the 
prescribed performance of the service braking 
system to be achieved and shall correspond to a 
vacuum not exceeding 90 percent ofthe maximum 
vacuum furnished by the energy source. 


NOTE— The initial energy level shall be stated in the approval 
document. 


b 


wm 


The energy storage device(s) shall not be fed; in 
addition any energy storage device(s) for auxiliary 
equipment shall be isolated. 

c) In the case of a power-driven vehicle authorized 
to tow a trailer, the supply line shall be stopped 
and an energy storage device of 0.5 litre capacity 
shall be connected to the control line. After the test 
referred to in F-3.2.1 the vacuum level provided at 
the control line shall not have fallen below a level 
equivalent to one-half of the figure obtained at the 
first brake application. 


F-3.3 Trailers (Categories T1 and T2 Only) 


F-3.3.1 The energy storage devices (energy reservoirs) 
with which trailers are equipped shall be such that 
the vacuum level provided at the user points shall not 
have fallen below a level equivalent to one-half of the 
value obtained at the first brake application after a test 
comprising four full-stroke actuations of the trailer's 
service braking system. 


F-3.3.2 Testing shall be performed in conformity with 
the following requirements: 


a) The initial energy level in the energy storage 
device(s) shall be that specified by the 
manufacturer. It shall be such as to enable the 
prescribed performance of the service braking 
system to be achieved. 


NOTE— The initial energy level shall be stated in the approval 
document. 


b 


ma 


The energy storage device(s) shall not be fed; 
in addition, any energy storage device(s) for 
auxiliary equipment shall be isolated. 


F-4 CAPACITY OF ENERGY SOURCES 


F-4.1 General 


Starting from the ambient atmospheric pressure, the 
energy source shall be capable of achieving in the 
energy storage device(s), in 3 min, the initial level 
specified in F-3.2.2 (a). In the case of a power-driven 
vehicle to which the coupling of a trailer is authorized, 
the time taken to achieve that level in the conditions 
specified in F-4.2 shall not exceed 6 min. 


52 


F-4.2 Conditions of Measurement 


F-4.2.1 The speed of the vacuum source shall be: 


a) where the vacuum source is the vehicle engine, the 
engine speed obtained with the vehicle stationary, 
the neutral gear engaged and the engine idling; 


b 


wm 


where the vacuum source is a pump, the speed 
obtained with the engine running at 65 percent of 
the speed corresponding to its maximum power 
output; and 


c 


— 


where the vacuum source is a pump and the engine 
is equipped with a governor, the speed obtained 
with the engine running at 65 percent of the 
maximum speed allowed by the governor. 


F-4.2.2 Where, it is intended to couple to the power- 
driven vehicle a trailer whose service braking system 
is vacuum-operated, the trailer shall be represented by 
an energy storage device having a capacity V in litres 
determined by the formula V = 15 R, where R is the 
maximum permissible mass, in tonnes, on the axles of 
the trailer. 


SECTION C HYDRAULIC BRAKING 
TEMS WITH STORED ENERGY 


SYS- 


F-5 CAPACITY OF ENERGY STORAGE DE- 
VICES (ENERGY RESERVOIRS) 


F-5.1 General 


F-5.1.1 Vehicles on which operation of the braking 
system requires the use of stored energy provided by 
hydraulic fluid under pressure shall be equipped with 
energy storage devices (energy reservoirs) of a capacity 
meeting the requirements of F-5.2. 


F-5.1.2 However, the energy storage devices shall not 
be required to be ofa prescribed capacity, if the braking 
system is such that in the absence of any energy reserve 
it is possible with the service braking system control 
to achieve a braking performance at least equal to that 
prescribed for the secondary braking system. 


F-5.1.3 In verifying compliance with the requirements 
of F-5.2.1, F-5.2.2 and F-6.1, the brakes shall be 
adjusted as closely as possible and for F-5.2.1, the rate 
of full-stroke actuations shall be such as to provide an 
interval of at least 60 s between each actuation. 


F-5.2 Power-Driven Vehicles 


F-5.2.1 Power-driven vehicles equipped with a 
hydraulic braking system with stored energy shall meet 
the following requirements: 


a) After eight full-stroke actuations of the service 
braking system control, it shall still be possible to 


achieve, on the ninth application, the performance 
prescribed for the secondary braking system; and 


b) Testing shall be performed in conformity with the 
following requirements: 


1) Testing shall commence at a pressure that may 
be specified by the manufacturer but is not 
higher than the cut-in pressure; and 


2) The energy storage device(s) shall not be fed; 
in addition, any energy storage device(s) for 
auxiliary equipment shall be isolated. 


F-5.2.2 Power-driven vehicles equipped with a 
hydraulic braking system with stored energy which 
cannot meet the requirements of 5.2.1.5.1 shall be 
deemed to satisfy if the following requirements are met: 


a) After any single transmission failure it shall still 
be possible after eight full-stroke actuations of 
the service braking system control, to achieve, 
at the ninth application, at least the performance 
prescribed for the secondary braking system or, 
where secondary performance requiring the use of 
stored energy is achieved by a separate control, 
it shall still be possible after eight full-stroke 
actuations to achieve, at the ninth application, the 
residual performance prescribed in 5.2.1.4. 


b 


ме 


Testing shall be performed in conformity with the 
following requirements: 


1) With the energy source stationary or operating 
at a speed corresponding to the engine idling 
speed, any transmission failure may be 
induced. Before inducing such a failure, the 
energy storage device(s) shall be at a pressure 
that may be specified by the manufacturer but 
not exceeding the cut-in pressure; and 


2 


wa 


The auxiliary equipment and its energy storage 
devices, if any, shall be isolated. 


F-6 CAPACITY OF HYDRAULIC FLUID EN- 
ERGY SOURCES 


F-6.1 The energy sources shall meet the requirements 
set out in the following paragraphs: 


53 


IS 11852 : 2019 


F-6.1.1 Definitions 


F-6.1.1.1 ‘p; represents the maximum system 
operational pressure (cut-out pressure) in the energy 
storage device(s) specified by the manufacturer. 


F-6.1.1.2 ‘p, represents the pressure after four full- 
stroke actuations with the service braking system 
control, starting at p,, without having fed the energy 
storage device(s). 


Е-6.1.1.3 ‘t’ represents the time required for the 
pressure to rise from p, to p, in the energy storage 
device(s) without application of the service braking 
system control. 


F-6.1.2 Conditions of Measurement 


F-6.1.2.1 During the test to determine the time t, the 
feed rate of the energy source shall be that obtained 
when the engine is running at the speed corresponding 
to its maximum power or at the speed allowed by the 
over-speed governor. 


F-6.1.2.2 During the test to determine the time ¢, energy 
storage device(s) for auxiliary equipment shall not be 
isolated other than automatically. 


F-6.1.3 Interpretation of Results 


F-6.1.3.1 In the case of all vehicles except those of 
categories M3, N2 and N3, the time t shall not exceed 
20 s. 


F-6.1.3.2 In the case of vehicles of categories M3, N2 
апа N3, the time ¢ shall not exceed 30 s. 


F-7 CHARACTERISTICS OF WARNING DE- 
VICES 


With the engine stationary and commencing at a 
pressure that may be specified by the manufacturer but 
does not exceed the cut-in pressure, the warning device 
shall not operate following two full-stroke actuations of 
the service braking system control.
