T-2.3.3.2 The manufacturer shall declare the brake 
chamber threshold pressure (p,.) and it shall be verified 
that when this pressure is applied the pushrod stroke 
defined in T-2.3.3 is produced. 


T-2.3.4 With respect to the verification of effective 
stroke (sp) - р), the measured value shall not be 
less than — 4 percent of the S, characteristics at the 
manufacturer’s declared pressure range. This value 
shall be recorded and specified in item 3.3.1 of T-6. 
Outside of this pressure range the tolerance may exceed 
- 4 percent. 


T-2.3.5 The test results recorded shall be reported on 
a form, a model of which is shown in T-7 and shall be 
included with the verification report, detailed in T-2.4. 


T-2.4 Verification Report 


T-2.4.1 The manufacturer’s declared performance 
characteristics, verified by the test results recorded in 
accordance with T-2.3.2 shall be reported on a form, a 
model of which is shown in T-6. 


T-3 PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS 
FOR SPRING BRAKES 


T-3.1 General 


T-3.1.1 This section defines the procedure by which the 
thrust/stroke/pressure characteristics are determined for 
spring brakes (see Note) that are used in compressed 
air braking systems to generate forces required in 
brakes with mechanical actuation. For the purpose of 
this verification procedure the spring brake section of 
a combined spring brake actuator is considered to be a 
spring brake. 

NOTE — Other spring brake designs may be approved upon 

presentation of equivalent information. 


T-3.1.2 The performance characteristics declared by the 
manufacturer shall be used in all calculations relating 
to the parking braking performance requirements of 
Annex U. 


T-3.2 Test Procedure 


T-3.2.1 Zero datum position of the spring brake 
chamber is to be taken as the fully pressurized position. 


T-3.2.2 In nominal stroke increments of < 10 mm, the 
corresponding thrust generated is to be monitored over 
the full stroke range available at zero pressure. 


T-3.2.3 The pressure shall then be gradually increased 
until the stroke is 10 mm from the zero datum position, 
and this pressure, defined as the release pressure, shall 
be recorded. 


T-3.2.4 The pressure shall then be increased to 850 kPa 
(8.5 bar), or the maximum working pressure declared 
by the manufacturer, whichever is lower. 


T-3.3 Verification 


T-3.3.1 With reference to T-8 (items 2.1, 3.1, 3.2 and 
3.3), a minimum of 6 samples shall be tested; with a 
verification report being issued providing the following 
conditions are met: 


T-3.3.1.1 Over a range of stroke from 10 mm to 2/3 
of the maximum stroke, no one result, measured 
in accordance with T-3.2.2, deviates by more than 
6 percent from the declared characteristics. 


T-3.3.1.2 No one result, measured in accordance with 
T-3.2.3, exceeds the declared value. 


129 


IS 11852 : 2019 


T-3.3.1.3 Each spring brake continues to function 
correctly after completion of the test in accordance 
with T-3.2.4. 


T-3.3.2 The test results recorded shall be reported on 
a form, a model of which is shown in T-9 and shall 
be included with the verification report detailed within 
T-3.4. 


T-3.4 Verification Report 


The manufacturer's declared performance 
characteristics, verified by the test results recorded in 
accordance with T-3.3.2 shall be reported on a form, a 
model of which is shown in T-8. 


T-4 COLD PERFORMANCE CHARACTERIS- 
TICS FOR TRAILER BRAKES 


T-4.1 General 


T-4.1.1 This procedure covers the testing of the ‘cold’ 
performance characteristics of air operated S cam and 
disc brakes (see Note) fitted to trailers. 


NOTE- Other brake designs may be approved upon 
presentation of equivalent information. 


T-4.1.2 The performance characteristics declared by the 
manufacturer shall be used for all calculations relating 
to the braking compatibility requirements of Annex J 
and to the Type 0 cold service braking and parking 
braking performance requirements of Annex U. 


T-4.2 Brake Factor and Brake Threshold Torque 


T-4.2.1 The preparation of the brake shall be in 
accordance with T-4.4.2. 


T-4.2.2 The brake factor is determined by using the 
following formula: 


. AOutput torque 


В: = 


A Input torque 


and shall be verified for each of the lining or pad 
materials specified in 4.3.1.3. 


T-4.2.3 The brake threshold torque shall be expressed 
in a manner that remains valid for variations of brake 
actuation and is denoted by the symbol C,. 


Т-4.2.4 The values of B, shall remain valid for 
variations of the following parameters: 


T-4.2.4.1 Mass per brake up to that defined in T-4.3.1.5. 


T-4.2.4.2 Dimensions and characteristics of external 
components used to actuate the brake. 


T-4.2.4.3 Wheel size/tyre dimensions. 


T-4.3 Information Document 


T-4.3.1 The brake manufacturer shall provide the test 
agency with at least the following information: 


T-4.3.1.1 A description of the brake type, model, size 
etc. 


T-4.3.1.2 Details of the brake geometry 


T-4.3.1.3 The make and type of brake lining(s) or brake 
pad(s) 


T-4.3.1.4 The brake drum or brake disc material 


T-4.3.1.5 The maximum technically permitted mass for 
the brake 


T-4.3.2 Additional Information 
T-4.3.2.1 Wheel and tyre sizes to be used for the test 
Т-4.3.2.2 The declared brake factor В, 


Т-4.3.2.3 The declared threshold torque C, ge 


T-4.4 Test Procedure 
T-4.4.1 Preparation 


T-4.4.1.1 A graph defining the acceptable performance 
variation shall be constructed, following the model 
shown in Fic. 24, using the manufacturers declared 
brake factor. 


T-4.4.1.2 The performance of the device used to actuate 
the brake shall be calibrated within an accuracy of 
1 percent. 


T-4.4.1.3 The dynamic tyre radius at the test loading 
shall be determined as prescribed for the test method. 


T-4.4.2 Bedding in (Burnishing) Procedure 


T-4.4.2.1 In the case of drum brakes the tests shall start 
with new brake linings and new drum(s), the brake 
linings shall be machined to achieve the best possible 
initial contact between the linings and drum(s). 


T-4.4.2.2 In the case of disc brakes the tests shall start 
with new brake pads and new disc(s), machining of 
the pad material shall be at the discretion of the brake 
manufacturer. 


T-4.4.2.3 Make 20 brake applications from an initial 
speed of 60 km/h with an input to the brake theoretically 
equal to 0.3 TR/Test Mass. The initial temperature at 
the lining/drum or pad/disc interface shall not exceed 
100 °C before each brake application. 


130 


BRAKINC RATE (z)(IE/(TEST M A 55)) 


IS 11852 : 2019 


PARALLEL 


BRAKE INPUT - (FORCE (N)) 
Fic. 24 ACCEPTABLE PERFORMANCE VARIATION 


T-4.4.2.4 Carry out 30 brake applications from 60 km/h 
to 30 km/h with an input to the brake equal to 0.3 TR/ 
Test Mass and with a time interval between applications 
of 60 s (see Note). The initial temperature at the lining/ 
drum or pad/disc interface on the first brake application 
shall not exceed 100 °C. 


NOTE- If the track test method or the rolling road test 
methods are to be utilised, energy inputs equivalent to those 
specified shall be used. 


T-4.4.2.5 On completion of the 30 brake applications 
defined in T-4.4.2.4 and after an interval of 120 s carry 
out 5 brake applications from 60 km/h to 30 km/h with 
an input to the brake equal to 0.3 TR/test mass and with 
an interval of 120 s between applications (see Note 
under T-4.4.2.4). 


T-4.4.2.6 Make 20 brake applications from an initial 
speed of 60 km/h with an input to the brake equal to 0.3 
TR/test mass. The initial temperature at the lining/drum 


or pad/disc interface shall not exceed 150?C before 
each brake application. 


T-4.4.2.7 Carry out a performance check as follows: 


T-4.4.2.7.1 Determine the input torque to produce 
theoretical performance values equivalent to 0.2, 0.35 
and 0.5 + 0.05 TR/Test Mass. 


T-4.4.2.7.2 Once the input torque value has been 
determined for each braking rate, this value shall 
remain constant throughout each and subsequent brake 
applications (for example constant pressure). 


T-4.4.2.7.3 Make a brake application with each of the 
input torques determined in T-4.4.2.7.1 from an initial 
speed of 60 km/h. The initial temperature at the lining/ 
drum or pad/disc interfaces shall not exceed 100°C 
before each application. 


131 


IS 11852 : 2019 


T-4.4.2.8 Repeat the procedures defined in T-4.4.2.6 
and T-4.4.2.7.3 above until the performance of five 
consecutive non-monotonic measurements at each 
constant input value has stabilized within a tolerance of 
+ 5 -10 percent of the maximum value. 


T-4.4.2.9 If the manufacturer can demonstrate by field 
test results, that the brake factor after this bedding 
in state is different from the brake factor which has 
developed on the road, additional conditioning is 
permissible. 


The maximum brake temperature, measured at the 
lining/drum or pad/disc interface, during this additional 
bedding in procedure shall not exceed 500 °C in the 
case of drum brakes and 700?C in the case of disc 
brakes. 


This field test shall be an endurance run with the same 
type and model of brake as that to be recorded in K-4, 
test report. The results of at least 3 tests in accordance 
with T-4.4.3.4 conducted under the conditions of the 
laden Type-0 test, during the field test, shall be the 
basis for determining whether further conditioning is 
permissible. The brake tests shall be documented as 
prescribed in T-15. 


The details of any additional conditioning shall be 
recorded and appended to the brake factor B, in 
K-4.2.3.1, by specifying for instance the following test 
parameters: 


a) Brake actuator pressure, the brake input torque or 
the brake output torque of the brake application; 

b) Speed at the beginning and the end of the brake 
application; 

c) Time in the case of a constant speed; and 

d) Temperature at the beginning and the end of the 


brake application or the duration of the brake 
cycle. 


T-4.4.2.10 In the case of this procedure being carried 
out on an inertia dynamometer or rolling road, unlimited 
use of cooling air is permitted. 


T-4.4.3 Verification Test 


Т-4.4.3.1 The temperature measured at the lining/drum 
or pad/disc interface shall not exceed 100 °C, at the 
start of each brake application. 


T-4.4.3.2 The brake threshold torque shall be 
determined from the measured value of brake input by 
reference to a calibrated input device. 


T-4.4.3.3 The initial speed for all brake applications is 
60 + 2 km/h. 


T-4.4.3.4 A minimum of six consecutive brake 
applications shall be made from 0.15 to 0.55 TR/test 


mass at ascending increments of application pressure, 
following by six brake applications made with the same 
application pressures in descending increments. 


T-4.4.3.5 For each of the brake applications in T-4.4.3.4 
the braking rate 1s calculated, corrected to take account 
of rolling resistance, and plotted on the graph specified 
in T-4.4.1.1. 


T-4.5 Test Methods 
T-4.5.1 Track Test 


T-4.5.1.1 The brake performance test shall be carried 
out on a single axle only. 


T-4.5.1.2 The tests shall be carried out on a straight 
level track, with a surface affording good adhesion, and 
performed when there is no wind liable to affect the 
results. 


T-4.5.1.3 The trailer shall be loaded (as closely as 
possible) to the maximum technically permitted mass 
for each brake, however, additional mass may be 
added if required to ensure that sufficient mass is over 
the axle under test to achieve a braking rate of 0.55 
TR/(maximum technically permitted mass per brake) 
without wheel lock. 


T-4.5.1.4 The dynamic rolling radius of the tyre may 
be verified at low speed, « 10 km/h, by measuring the 
distance travelled as a function wheel revolutions, the 
minimum number of revolutions required to determine 
the dynamic rolling radius is 10. 


T-4.5.1.5 The rolling resistance of the vehicle 
combination is to be determined by measuring the 
time taken for the vehicle speed to reduce from 55 to 
45 km/h and the distance covered, when tested in the 
same direction in which the verification test will be 
carried out and with the engine disconnected and any 
endurance brake system disengaged. 


T-4.5.1.6 Only the brakes of the axle under test shall 
be actuated and reach an input pressure at the brake 
input device of 90 + 3 percent (after maximum build 
up time of 0.7 s) of its asymptotic value. The test shall 
be carried out with the engine disconnected and any 
endurance braking system disengaged. 


T-4.5.1.7 The brakes shall be closely adjusted at the 
start of the test. 


T-4.5.1.8 The brake input for the purpose of calculating 
the brake threshold torque shall be determined by 
lifting the wheel and gradually applying the brake 
whilst the wheel is rotated by hand until resistance is 
detected. 


132 


T-4.5.1.9 The final speed v, shall be calculated by the 
following formula: 


„= PI RPSL 

Where, 

v,— initial speed, km/h; 

v, — final speed, km/h; 

P, — mass of the towing vehicle under test conditions, 
in kg; 

P, = part ofthe mass of the trailer borne by the unbraked 
axle(s), in kg; and 

P, = part of the mass of the trailer borne by the braked 
axle(s), in kg. 


T-4.5.1.10 The braking performance of the axle under 
test shall be determined by calculating the deceleration 
determined from a direct measurement of velocity and 
distance between 0.8 v, and v,, where v, shall not be 
less than 0.1 v,. This shall be deemed to be equivalent 
to the mean fully developed deceleration (MFDD) as 
defined in Annex C. 


T-4.5.2 Inertia Dynamometer Test 


T-4.5.2.1 The test shall be carried out on a single brake 
assembly. 


T-4.5.2.2 The test machine shall be capable of 
generating the inertia required by T-4.5.2.5. 


T-4.5.2.3 The test machine shall be calibrated for speed 
and brake output torque within an accuracy of 2 percent. 


T-4.5.2.4 The instrumentation for the test shall be 
capable of providing at least the following data: 


a) A continuous recording of brake application 
pressure or force; 


b) A continuous recording of brake output torque; 


c) A continuous recording of the temperature 
measured at the lining/drum or pad/disc interface; 
and 


d) Speed during the test. 


Т-4.5.2.5 The inertia (Z) of the dynamometer 
shall be set as close аз possible, with 
+ 5 percent tolerance, including the internal friction 
of the dynamometer, to that part of the linear inertia 
of the vehicle acting upon one wheel necessary for 
a performance of 0.557R/maximum technically 
permitted mass according to the following formula: 


„= Рак? 
Where, 
I, = actual rotary inertia, in kgm’; 
R = tyre rolling radius defined by the formula 


0.485 D; 


IS 11852 : 2019 


D = d+2H (see Note); 
d — rim diameter conventional number, in mm; 
H = nominal section height, in mm = S, x 0.01 Ra; 
S, — section width, in mm; 
Ra = nominal aspect ratio; and 
Pd = maximum technically permitted mass/brake 


as defined in T-4.3.1.5. 


NOTE — Outer diameter of tyre, as defined in IS 15633 and 
IS 15636 


T-4.5.2.6 Cooling air at ambient temperature may be 
used, flowing at a velocity not exceeding 0.33 v over 
the brake in a direction perpendicular to its axis of 
rotation. 


T-4.5.2.7 The brake shall be closely adjusted at the start 
of the test. 


T-4.5.2.8 The brake input for the purpose of calculating 
the brake threshold torque shall be determined by 
gradually applying the brake until the onset of brake 
torque generation is observed. 


T-4.5.2.9 The brake performance shall be determined 
by applying the following formula to the measured 
brake output torque 


Braking rate = мл 
Where, 
M, — average brake output torque (Nm) - based on 
distance; 
Ig = deceleration due to gravity (m/s?); and 
R = tyre rolling radius defined by the formula 


0.485 D. 


The average brake output torque (М) shall be 
calculated from the deceleration determined from a 
direct measurement of velocity and distance between 
0.8 v, and 0.1 v, This shall be deemed to be equivalent 
to the mean fully developed deceleration (MFDD) as 
defined in Annex C. 


T-4.5.3 Rolling Road Test 


T-4.5.3.1 The test shall be carried out on single axle 
with one or two brakes. 


T-4.5.3.2 The test machine shall have a calibrated 
means of imposing load to simulate the required mass 
for the brake(s) to be tested. 


T-4.5.3.3 The test machine shall be calibrated for 
speed and brake torque within an accuracy of 2 percent 
taking into account the internal friction characteristics. 
The dynamic rolling radius of the tyre (R) shall be 
determined by measuring the rotational speed of the 


133 


IS 11852 : 2019 


rolling road and the unbraked wheels of the axle under 
test at a speed equivalent to 60 km/h, and calculated by 
the formula: 


R-Rza Вр 
nw 
Where, 
R, — radius ofthe rolling road, 
ny = rotational speed of rolling road, and 
n, = rotational speed of the unbraked wheels of the 


axle. 


T-4.5.3.4 Cooling air at ambient temperature may be 
used, flowing at a velocity not exceeding 0.33 v over 
the brake(s). 


T-4.5.3.5 The brake(s) shall be closely adjusted at the 
start of the test. 


T-4.5.3.6 The brake input for the purpose of calculating 
the brake threshold torque shall be determined by 
gradually applying brake(s) until the onset of brake 
torque generation is observed. 


T-4.5.3.7 The brake performance shall be determined 
by measuring the brake force at the periphery of the 
tyre calculated to braking rate, taking into account the 
rolling resistance. The rolling resistance of the loaded 
axle will be determined by measuring the force at the 
periphery of the tyre at a speed of 60 km/h. 


The average brake output torque (M) shall be based 
on the measured values between the moment, the 
application pressure/force reaches its asymptotic value 
from the onset of pressure rise at the brake input device 
and when the energy input has reached the value W,, 
that is defined in T-4.5.3.8. 


T-4.5.3.8 For determining the braking rate, an energy 
input W equivalent to the kinetic energy of the 
corresponding mass for the brake under test when 
braked from 60 km/h to standstill, shall be taken into 
account.

T-4.5.3.8.1 If the test speed v cannot be maintained at 
60 + 2 km/h during the measurement of the braking

determined from the direct measurement of brake 
force F, and/or brake output torque M, so that the 
measurement of this/these parameter(s) are not affected 
by the dynamic forces of the inertia mass of the rolling 
road test machine. 


T-4.6 Verification Report 


T-4.6.1 The manufacturer’s declared performance 
characteristics, verified by the test results recorded in 
accordance with T-4.4.3 shall be reported. 


T-5 ANTI-LOCK BRAKING SYSTEMS (ABS) 
T-5.1 General 


T-5.1.1 This paragraph defines the procedure to 
determine the performance ofa trailer anti-lock braking 
system. 


T-5.1.2 Tests carried out on trailers of category T4 
will be deemed to cover the requirements for trailers 
of T3 category. 


T-5.2 Information Document 


The manufacturer of the ABS shall supply to the Test 
Agency an information document of the system(s) 
requiring performance verification. This document 
shall contain at least the information defined in T-10 12. 


T-5.3 Definition of Test Vehicles 


T-5.3.1 Based on the information supplied in the 
information document, in particular the trailer applications 
defined in item 2.1 of T-10, the test agency shall carry 
out tests on representative trailers having up to three 
axles and equipped with the respective anti-lock braking 
system/configuration. Additionally, when selecting 
trailers for evaluation consideration shall also be given to 
the parameters defined in the following paragraphs. 


T-5.3.1.1 Suspension type 


The method of evaluating the performance of the anti- 
lock braking system relative to the suspension type will 
be selected in the following way: 


a) Semi-trailers — For each suspension group for 
example balanced mechanical etc. a representative 
trailer shall be evaluated; and 


b) Full trailers — Evaluation to be carried out on 
a representative trailer equipped with any one 
suspension type. 


T-5.3.1.2 Wheelbase 


For semi-trailers the wheelbase shall not be a limiting 
factor, but for full trailers the shortest wheelbase shall 
be evaluated. 


T-5.3.1.3 Brake type 


Approval shall be limited to S cam or disc brakes but 
should other types become available then comparative 
testing may be required. 


134 


T-5.3.1.4 Load sensing device 


The utilization of adhesion shall be determined with the 
load sensing valve set to laden and unladen conditions. 
In all cases the requirements of M-2.7 shall apply. 


T-5.3.1.5 Brake actuation 


Differentials in the level of actuation shall be recorded 
for evaluation during the tests to determine the 
utilization of adhesion. Results obtained from tests for 
one trailer may be applied to other trailers of the same 


type. 


T-5.3.2 Foreachtype oftrailerundertest, documentation 
showing brake compatibility as defined in Annex J 
(Fig. 7 and 9) shall be made available to demonstrate 
conformity. 


T-5.3.3 For the purpose of the approval, semi-trailers 
and centre axle trailers shall be deemed to be of the 
same vehicle type. 


T-5.4 Test Schedule 


T-5.4.1 The following tests shall be conducted by the 
Test Agency on the vehicle(s) defined in T-5.3 for 
each ABS configuration taking into consideration the 
application list defined in 2.1 of T-10. However, worst 
case cross referencing may eliminate certain tests. If 
worst case testing is actually used, this should be stated 
in the test report. 


T-5.4.1.1 Utilization of Adhesion 


Tests shall be carried out according to the procedure 
defined in M-6.2 or each ABS configuration and trailer 
type, as defined in the manufacturer’s information 
document (see item 2.1 of T-10). 


T-5.4.1.2 Energy consumption 


T-5.4.1.2.1 Axle loading 


The trailer(s) to be tested shall be loaded so that the 
axle load is 2500 + 200 kg or 35 percent + 200 kg of 
the permissible static axle load whichever is the lower. 


T-5.4.1.2.2 It shall be ensured that ‘full cycling’ of the 
anti-lock braking system can be achieved throughout 
the dynamic tests defined in M-6.1.3. 


T-5.4.1.2.3 Energy consumption test 


The test shall be carried out according to the procedure 
defined in M-6.1 for each ABS configuration. 


T-5.4.1.2.4 To enable trailers submitted for approval 
to be checked for conformity to the anti-lock energy 
consumption requirements (see M-6.1), the following 
checks shall be carried out: 


IS 11852 : 2019 


T-5.4.1.2.4.1 Prior to the commencement of the energy 
consumption test (T-5.4.1.2.3) in the case of brakes 
with non integrated brake wear adjustment the brakes 
shall be set to a condition where the relationship (А) of 
brake chamber push rod travel (у) against lever length 
(1) is 0.2. This relationship shall be determined for a 
brake chamber pressure of 650 kPa (6.5 bar). 


Example, l, = 130 mm, s, at 650 kPa brake chamber 
pressure — 26 mm 


R,75,/1,7 26/130 = 0.2 


In the case of brakes with integrated automatic brake 
wear adjustment the brakes shall be set to the normal 
running clearance specified by the manufacturer. 


Setting of the brakes as defined above shall be carried 
out when the brakes are cold (« 100°C). 


T-5.4.1.2.4.2 With the load sensing valve set to the laden 
condition and the initial energy level set according to 
M-6.1.2 the energy storage device(s) shall be isolated 
from further supply of air. The brakes shall be applied 
with a control pressure of 650 kPa (6.5 bar) at the coupling 
head and then released. Further applications shall be 
made until the pressure in the brake chambers is the same 
as that obtained after following the test procedure defined 
in T-5.4.1.2.1 and T-5.4.1.2.2. The number of equivalent 
brake applications (л, ) shall be noted. 


The equivalent number of static brake applications (л) 
is to be recorded in the test report. 


Where, 


n = 1.2 . n, and is to be rounded up to the nearest 
whole integer 


T-5.4.1.3 Split friction test 


Where an anti-lock braking system is to be defined as 
category A system then all such ABS configurations 
shall be subject to the performance requirements of 
M-6.3.2. 


T-5.4.1.4 Low and high speed performance 


T-5.4.1.4.1 With the trailer set as for utilization of 
adhesion evaluation, verification of the low and high 
speed performance shall be carried out according to 
M-6.3.1. 


T-5.4.1.4.2 Where a tolerance exists between the number 
of exciter teeth and tyre circumference, functional 
checks shall be carried out at the extremes of tolerance 
in accordance with M-6.3. This may be achieved by 
utilizing different tyre sizes or by producing special 
exciters to simulate frequency extremes. 


T-5.4.1.5 Additional checks 


The following additional checks shall be carried 
out with the towing vehicle unbraked and the trailer 
unladen. 


135 


IS 11852 : 2019 


T-5.4.1.5.1 When the axle bogie passes from a high 
adhesion surface (К) to a low adhesion surface (k,) 
where К > 0.5 and &, / k, > 2, with a control pressure 
at the coupling head of 650 kPa (6.5 bar), the directly 
controlled wheels shall not lock. The running speed and 
the instant of applying the trailer brakes is so calculated 
that with the anti-lock braking system full cycling on 
the high adhesion surface, the passage from one surface 
to the other being made at approximately 80 km/h and 
at 40 km/h. 


T-5.4.1.5.2 When the trailer passes from a low adhesion 
surface (А) to a high adhesion surface (К) where К, 
> 0.5 and К. / К, > 2, with a control pressure at the 
coupling head of 650 kPa (6.5 bar), the pressure at 
the brake chambers shall rise to an appropriate high 
value within a reasonable time and the trailer shall not 
deviate from its initial course. The running speed and 
the instant of applying the brakes is so calculated that, 
with the anti-lock braking system full cycling on the 
low adhesion surface, the passage from one surface to 
the other occurs at approximately 50 km/h. 


T-5.4.1.6 Documentation relating to the controller(s) 
shall be made available as required by 5.1.5 and M-4.1. 


T-5.5 Approval Report 


T-5.5.1 An approval report shall be produced, the 
content of which is defined in T-11. 


T-6 VEHICLE STABILITY FUNCTION 
T-6.1 General 


T-6.1.1 This section defines a test procedure to 
determine the dynamic characteristics of a vehicle 
equipped with a vehicle stability function consisting of 
at least one of the following functions: 


(a) Directional control; and 
(b) Roll-over control. 


T-6.2 Information Document 


The system/vehicle manufacturer shall supply to the 
test agency an information document of the control 
function(s) for which performance verification is 
required. This document shall contain at least the 
information defined in T-14. 


T-6.3 Definition of Test Vehicle(s) 


Based on the stability control function(s) and 
their application(s) defined in the manufacturer's 
information document the test agency shall carry out 
a performance verification. This may include one or 
more dynamic manoeuvres as defined in V-2.2.3 to 
this Regulation on a trailer(s) having up to three axles 
which is representative of the application(s) defined in 


T-14.2.1. 


T-6.3.1 When selecting the trailer(s) for evaluation, 
consideration shall also be given to the following: 


a) Suspension type: for each suspension group, for 
example, balanced pneumatic, a trailer of that 
specification shall be evaluated; 


b) Wheel base: wheel base shall not be a limiting 
factor; 


c) Brake type: approval shall be limited to trailers 
with S-cam or disc brakes but should other types 
become available, then comparative testing may 
be required; and 


d) Braking system: the braking system of the 
trailer(s) to be evaluated shall comply with all of 
the relevant requirements of this Regulation. 


T-6.4 Test Schedule 


To evaluate the vehicle stability control function the 
tests used shall be agreed between the system/vehicle 
manufacturer and the test agency and shall include 
conditions, appropriate to the function being evaluated, 
that would without the intervention of the stability 
control function result in loss of directional control or 
roll-over. The dynamic manoeuvres, test conditions and 
results shall be included in the test report. 


T-6.5 Towing Vehicle 


The towing vehicle used for evaluating the performance 
of the vehicle (trailer) stability function shall have 
the necessary pneumatic and electrical connections 
and if the towing vehicle is equipped with a vehicle 
stability function as defined in 3.34 that function shall 
be disabled. 


T-6.6 Test Report 


A test report shall be produced, the content of which 
shall be at least that defined in T-15. 


PART 2 PERFORMANCE TESTING OF MO- 
TOR VEHICLE BRAKING COMPONENTS 


T-7 GENERAL 


Part 2 defines the procedures applicable in defining the 
performance of the following. 


T-7.1 A Vehicle Stability Function 


T-7.1.1 General 


This section defines the procedure of determining the 
dynamic characteristics of a vehicle equipped with a 
vehicle stability function as specified in 5.2.1.32. 


T-7.1.2 Information Document 


The system manufacturer shall supply the test agency 
with an information document on the vehicle stability 


136 


control function(s) for which performance verification 
is required. This document shall contain at least the 
information defined in T-18 and shall be attached as an 
appendix to the test report. 


T-7.1.3 Definition of Test Vehicle(s) 


T-7.1.3.1 Based on the stability control function(s) and 
their application(s) defined in the system manufacturer's 
information document, the test agency shall carry out 
a vehicle based performance verification. This shall 
include one or more dynamic manoeuvres as defined in 
V-2.1.3 on a motor vehicle(s) which is representative of 
the application(s) defined in paragraph T-14.2.1 of the 
system manufacturer information document. 


T-7.1.1.3.2 When selecting the motor vehicles(s) for 
evaluation, consideration shall also be given to the 
following: 


a) Braking system: the braking system of the test 
vehicle(s) to be evaluated shall comply with all of 
the relevant requirements of this Regulation; 

b) Vehicle category — М„ M,, N, №; 

c) Character of the vehicle; 

d) Vehicle configuration(s) (for example, 4 х 2, 6 x 2, 
etc.): each configuration to be evaluated; 

e) Drive orientation (left or right hand drive): not a 
limiting factor — Evaluation not required; 

f) Single front axle steering: not a limiting factor — 
Evaluation not required (see subparagraphs (g) 
and (h)); 

g) Additional steering axles (for example, forced 
steering, self-steering): to be evaluated; 

h) Steering ratio: to be evaluated — End-of-line 
programming or self-learning systems not a 
limiting factor; 

j) Drive axles: to be taken into consideration with 
regard to the use (loss) of wheel speed sensing in 
the determination of vehicle speed; 

k) Lift axles: lift axle detection/control and lifted 
condition to be evaluated; 

m) Engine management: communication 
compatibility to be evaluated; 

n) Gearbox type (for example, manual, automated 
manual, semi-automatic, automatic) to be 
evaluated; 

p) Drive train options (for example, retarder): to be 
evaluated; 

q) Differential type (for example standard or self- 
locking): to be evaluated; 

r) Differential lock(s) (driver selected): 
evaluated; 


to be 


s) Brake system type (for example, air over hydraulic, 
full air): to be evaluated; 


IS 11852 : 2019 


t) Brake type (disc, drum (single wedge, twin wedge, 
S-cam)): not a limiting factor, however, should 
other types become available, then comparative 
testing may be required; 

u) Anti-lock braking configurations: to be evaluated; 

v) Wheelbase: to be evaluated 


In the case where vehicles conforming to the minimum 
and maximum  wheelbases as specified in the 
information document are not available at the time of 
testing, minimum and maximum wheelbase verification 
may be carried-out using system manufacturer test data 
for real vehicles with a wheelbase within 20 per cent of 
the actual minimum and maximum wheelbase vehicles 
being tested by the test agency; 


x) Wheel type (single or twin): to be covered in the 
system manufacturer's information document; 


y) Tyre type (for example, structure, category of use, 
size): to be covered in the system manufacturer's 
information document; 


Z) Track width: not a limiting factor — covered by 
variations in the centre of gravity evaluation; 


aa) Suspension type (for example, air, mechanical, 
rubber): to be evaluated; 


ab) Centre of gravity height: to be evaluated 


In the case where vehicles conforming to the 
maximum centre of gravity height as specified 
in the information document are not available at 
the time of testing, maximum centre of gravity 
height verification may be carried-out utilising 
system manufacturer's test data for real vehicles 
with a centre of gravity height within +20 per 
cent of the actual maximum centre of gravity 
height of the vehicles being tested by the test 
agency; 

ac 


wm 


Lateral acceleration sensor position: installation 
envelop as specified by the system manufacturer 
to be evaluated; 


ad) Yaw rate sensor position: installation envelop 
as specified by the system manufacturer to be 


evaluated. 


T-7.1.1.4 Test schedule 


T-7.1.1.4.1 To evaluate the vehicle stability control 
function, the tests used shall be agreed upon between 
the system manufacturer and the test agency and shall 
include conditions, appropriate to the function being 
evaluated, that would without the intervention of the 
stability control function result in loss of directional 
control or roll-over control. The dynamic manoeuvres, 
test conditions and results shall be included in the test 
report. 


The evaluation shall include the following, as 
appropriate: 


137 


IS 11852 : 2019 


T-7.1.1.4.1.1 Additional steering axles 


Evaluate the influence by a comparison of results 
with the axle in its normal steering mode and with the 
steering disabled so that it becomes a fixed axle, unless 
it is an end-of-line programming parameter. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.2 Steering ratio 


Tests to be carried-out to determine the effectiveness 
of any end-of-line programming or self-learning using 
a number of vehicles with different steering ratios, or 
the approval is restricted to the steering ratios actually 
tested. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.3 Lift axle 


Tests to be carried-out with the lift axle in the raised and 
lowered conditions, with position detection and signal 
transfer being evaluated to establish that the change in 
wheelbase has been recognized. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.4 Engine management 


Control of the engine, or any other source(s) of motive 
power, to be shown to be independent from driver 
demand. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.5 Drive train options 


The effect of any options to be shown, for example, 
retarder management to be independent of the driver in 
the case of a retarder. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.6 Differential type/differential lock(s) 


Effect of self-locking or driver selected locking to be 
shown, for example, function maintained, reduced or 
switched-off. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.7 Anti-lock braking configurations 


Each anti-lock braking configuration shall be tested on 
at least one vehicle. 


If the vehicle stability function is hosted on different 
systems (for example, ABS, EBS), tests shall be carried- 
out on vehicles having the different hosting systems. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.8 Suspension type 


Vehicles shall be selected on the basis of the suspension 
type (for example, air, mechanical, rubber) of each axle 
or axle group. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.9 Centre of gravity height 


Tests shall be carried-out on vehicles where it is 
possible to adjust the centre of gravity height so as to 
demonstrate that the roll-over control is able to adapt to 
changes in the centre of gravity height. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.10 Lateral acceleration sensor position 


The effect of the lateral acceleration sensor being 
installed in different positions on the same vehicle 
shall be evaluated to confirm the installation envelop 
specified by the system manufacturer. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.11 Yaw rate sensor position 


The effect of the yaw rate sensor being installed 
in different positions on the same vehicle shall be 
evaluated to confirm the installation envelop specified 
by the system manufacturer. 


T-7.1.1.4.1.12 Loading 


Vehicles shall be tested in both the laden and unladen/ 
part laden conditions to demonstrate that the vehicle 
stability function is able to adapt to differing conditions 
of load. 

In the case of a semi-trailer tractor, tests shall be 
carried-out as follows: 

(a) With a coupled semi-trailer, in the laden and 
unladen/part laden conditions, in which the roll- 
over control, if fitted, has been disabled; 

(b) In the solo condition (without a coupled semi- 
trailer or imposed load); and 

(c) With a load simulating the laden condition 
(without a coupled semi-trailer). 


T-7.1.1.4.2 Evaluation of buses 


As an alternative, in the case of buses, trucks having 
the same braking system type may be used in the 
evaluation. However, at least one bus shall be included 
in the testing and the subsequent report. 


T-7.1.1.5 Test report 


T-7.1.1.5.1 A test report shall be produced, the content 
of which shall be at least that defined in T-19. 


138 


IS 11852 : 2019

T-16 SYMBOLS AND DEFINITIONS 


Symbol Definition 

B, Brake factor (input torque to output torque amplification ratio) 

C Threshold input torque (minimum torque necessary to produce a measurable brake torque) 

D Outer tyre diameter (overall diameter of an inflated new tyre) 

d A conventional number denoting the nominal rim diameter and corresponding to the diameter 
of the rim expressed either in inches or mm 

F; Brake force 

H Nominal tyre section height (the distance equal to half the difference between the outer diameter 
of the tyre and the nominal rim diameter) 

I Rotary inertia 

[. Brake lever length of reference test trailer 

M, Average brake output torque 


145 


IS 11852 : 2019 


Symbol Definition 

n. Equivalent number of static brake applications for the purpose of type approval 

n. Equivalent number of static applications obtained during testing 

ny Rotational speed of the rolling road 

ny, Rotational speed of the unbraked wheels of the axle 

Pd Maximum technically permitted mass for the brake 

р Pressure 

R Dynamic tyre rolling radius (calculated using 0.485D) 

Ra Nominal aspect ratio of the tyre (one hundred times the number obtained by dividing the 
number expressing the nominal section height of the tyre in mm by the number expressing the 
nominal section width in mm). 

RI Ratio of s, / [. 

Rg Radius of the rolling road 

S, Section width of the tyre (linear distance between the outsides of the sidewalls of an inflated 
tyre, excluding elevations due to labelling (marking), decorations or protective bands or ribs). 

S Actuator stroke (working stroke plus free stroke) 

Sus Total actuator stroke 

S, Effective stroke (the stroke at which the output thrust is 90 percent of the average thrust 7h,) 

Sy Brake chamber push rod travel of reference test trailer in mm 

Th Average thrust (the average thrust is determined by integrating the values between 1/3 and 2/3 
of the total stroke 5, ) (see Fig. 25) 

Th. Spring thrust of the spring brake 

TR Sum of braking forces at periphery of all wheels of trailer or semi-trailer 

V Rolling road test speed 

V, Initial speed, when braking starts 

y, Speed at end of braking 

Wn Energy input, equivalent to the kinetic energy of the corresponding mass for the brake under 
test when braked from 60 km/h to standstill 

Z Braking rate of vehicle 

Dis Pressure in the brake chamber required to produce a pushrod stroke of 15mm from the zero 


datum position.

ANNEX U 
( Clauses 6, T-1.2 and T-3.1.2 ) 


ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR 
THE TYPE APPROVAL OF TRAILERS 


U-1 GENERAL 


U-1.1 This Annex defines an alternative procedure 
for type approving trailers, utilising information from 
test reports issued in accordance with Annex K and 
Annex T. 


U-1.2 On completion of the verification procedures 
described in U-3 to U-8, the certifying agency/approval 
authority shall issue a type approval certificate 
conforming to the model specified in A-2. 


U-1.3 For the purposes of the calculations defined 
within this Annex the centre of gravity height shall be 
determined in accordance with the method defined in 
0-9. 


0-2 APPLICATION FOR TYPE APPROVAL 


U-2.1 The application for ECE type approval of a 
trailer type with regard to the braking equipment shall 
be submitted by the trailer manufacturer. In support of 
the approval the trailer manufacturer shall supply to the 
certifying agency at least the following. 


U-2.1.1 A copy of the ECE or EU type approval 
certificate and an information document of a trailer 
hereafter referred to as the "reference trailer" on 
which the service braking performance comparison is 
to be based. This trailer will have been subject to the 
actual tests defined in Annex C to this Standard for the 
appropriate trailer or equivalent EU Directive. A trailer 
that has been approved to the alternative procedure 
defined in this Annex shall not be used as a reference 
trailer. 


U-2.1.2 Copies of the Annex K and Annex T test 
reports. 


U-2.1.3 A documentation package that contains the 
relevant verification information including the relevant 
calculations for the following: 


Performance Requirements Reference to Clause 


Cold service braking performance U-3 
Parking brake performance U-4 
Emergency brake performance U-5 
Failure of brake distribution system U-6 
Anti-lock braking U-7 
Vehicle stability function U-8 
Functional check U-9 


U-2.1.4 A trailer, representative of the trailer type to be 
approved hereafter referred to as the ‘subject trailer’. 


U-2.2 The manufacturer of the ‘reference trailer’ and 
‘subject trailer’ shall be the same. 


U-3 ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR 
DEMONSTRATING THE TYPE 0 TEST SER- 
VICE BRAKING COLD PERFORMANCE 


U-3.1 To demonstrate compliance with the Type 0 test 
service braking cold performance it shall be verified, 
by calculation, that the ‘subject trailer’ has sufficient 
brake force (TR) available to achieve the prescribed 
service braking performance and that there is sufficient 
adhesion available on a dry road surface (assumed to 
have a coefficient of adhesion of 0.8) to utilize this 
brake force. 


U-3.2 Verification 


U-3.2.1 The requirements of C-1.2.7 and C-3.1.2 
(cold performance requirement and achievement 
without wheel lock, deviation or abnormal vibration) 
are considered to be satisfied by the subject trailer if it 
meets the verification criteria described in the following 
paragraphs, in both the laden and unladen conditions: 


U-3.2.1.1 The wheelbase of the subject trailer shall not 
be less than 0.8 times the reference trailer wheelbase. 


U-3.2.1.2 Any difference in the brake input torque 
between one axle and another within a bogie of 
the ‘subject trailer’ shall not differ from that of the 
‘reference trailer’. 


U-3.2.1.3 The number and arrangement of axles that 
is; lifting, steering, etc. of the ‘subject trailer’ shall not 
differ from that of the reference trailer. 


U-3.2.1.4 The percentage distribution of the laden static 
axle load of the subject trailer shall not differ from that 
of the reference trailer by more than 10 percent. 


U-3.2.1.5 For semi-trailers, a graph, in accordance with 
U-10, shall be constructed and from this graph, it shall 
be verified that, 


a) TR „> TR. [that is line (1) shall not be below 
line (3)]; an 

b) TR, > TR,, [that is line (2) shall not be below line 
(3)]. 


153 


IS 11852 : 2019 


U-3.2.1.6 For centre axle trailers, a graph, in accordance 
with U-11, shall be constructed and, from this graph, it 
shall be verified that, 


a) TR „> TR. [that is line (1) shall not be below 
line (3)], an 

b) TR, > IR. [that 1s line (2) shall not be below line 
(3)]. 


U-3.2.1.7 For full trailers, a graph, in accordance with 
U-12, shall be constructed and, from this graph, it shall 
be verified that, 


а) TR wx”? TR. [that is line (1) shall not be below 
line (2)], 

b) ТК „> DR [that is line (4) shall not be below line 
(3)], and 


с) ТК > TR [that is line (6) shall not be below line 
(5)]. 


U-4 ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR 
DEMONSTRATING THE PARKING BRAKE 
PERFORMANCE 


U-4.1 General 


U-4.1.1 This procedure provides an alternative to 
physically testing trailers on a gradient and ensures 
that trailers fitted with spring brake actuated parking 
mechanisms can meet the prescribed parking brake 
performance. This procedure shall not be applied to 
trailers fitted with parking mechanisms operated by 
means other than spring brakes. Such trailers shall be 
subjected to the physical test prescribed in Annex C. 


U-4.1.2 The prescribed parking braking performance 
shall be demonstrated by calculation, using the 
formulae contained in U-4.2 and U-4.3. 


U-4.2 Parking Performance 


U-4.2.1 The parking brake force at the periphery of 
the tyres of axle(s) braked by the spring brake actuated 
parking mechanism shall be calculated using the 
following formula:

0-5 ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR 
DEMONSTRATING THE EMERGENCY/ AU- 
TOMATIC BRAKING PERFORMANCE 


U-5.1 General 


To demonstrate compliance with the automatic braking 
performance requirements, either a comparison is made 
between the chamber pressure required to achieve the 
specified performance and the asymptotic chamber 
pressure after disconnection of the supply line, as 
defined in U-5.2.1, or it shall be verified that the brake 
force provided by the axle(s) fitted with spring brakes 
is sufficient to achieve the specified performance, as 
defined in U-5.2.2. 


U-5.2 Verification 


U-5.2.1 The requirements of C-3.3 are considered to be 
satisfied by a subject trailer, if the asymptotic chamber 
pressure (р) after disconnection of the supply line is 
greater than the chamber pressure (р) to achieve a 
performance of 13.5 percent of the maximum stationary 
wheel load. The supply line pressure being stabilized at 
700 kPa prior to disconnection. 


U-5.2.2 The requirements of C-3.3 are considered to be 
satisfied by a spring brake equipped subject trailer if: 


Tpi = 0.135 (PR)(g) 


where, T ie is calculated in accordance with U-4.2.1. 


U-6 ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR 
DEMONSTRATING BRAKING PERFOR- 
MANCE IN THE CASE OF FAILURE OF THE 
BRAKING DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM 


U-6.1 General 


To demonstrate compliance with the braking 
performance requirements in the case of a failure of 
the braking distribution system, a comparison is made 
between the chamber pressure required to achieve 
the specified performance and the chamber pressure 
available when a failure in the braking distribution 
system exists. 


U-6.2 Verification 


U-6.2.1 The requirements of J-6, are considered to be 
satisfied by the subject trailer if the pressure defined in 
U-6.2.1.1 is greater than or equal to the pressure defined 
in U-6.2.1.2., in both laden and unladen conditions. 


U-6.2.1.1 The chamber pressure (р) of the subject 
trailer, when р, = 650 kPa, the supply line pressure = 


IS 11852 : 2019 


700 kPa and a failure in the braking distribution system 
exists. 


U-6.2.1.2 The chamber pressure (р) to achieve a 
braking rate of 30 percent of the service braking 
performance prescribed for the subject trailer.

provided that the anti-lock braking system (ABS) 
complies with the requirements of Annex U. 


U-7.2 Verification

U-7.3 Verification of Reservoir Capacity 


U-7.3.1 As the range of braking systems and auxiliary 
equipment used on trailers is diverse it is not possible 
to have a table of recommended reservoir capacities. 
To verify that adequate storage capacity is installed, 
testing may be conducted according to M-6.1 or by the 
procedure defined below: 


U-7.3.1.1 In the case of brakes with non-integrated 
brake wear adjustment the brakes on the subject trailer 
shall be set to a condition where the relationship (R7) of 
brake chamber push rod travel (s,) against lever length 
(1) is 0.2. 


Example: 

{= 130 mm 

R = s/l 5/130-02 

s, = Push rod travel at 650 kPa brake chamber pressure 
= 130x 0.2 = 26 mm 


U-7.3.1.2 In the case of brakes with integrated 
automatic brake wear adjustment the brakes shall be 
set to a normal running clearance. 


U-7.3.1.3 Setting of the brakes as defined above shall 
be carried out when the brakes are cold (< 100 °C). 


U-7.3.1.4 With the brakes adjusted according to relevant 
procedure defined above and the load sensing device(s) 
set to the laden condition and the initial energy level 
set according to M-6.1.2, the energy storage device(s) 
shall be isolated from further supply. The brakes 
shall be applied with a control pressure of 650 kPa 
at the coupling head and then fully released. Further 
brake applications shall be made up to the number n, 
determined from the test conducted in accordance with 
T-5.4.1.2.4.2 and defined in 2.5 of the anti-lock braking 
system approval report. During this application, the 
pressure in the operating circuit shall be sufficient 
to provide a total braking force at the periphery of 
the wheels equal to not less than 22.5 percent of the 
maximum stationary wheel load and without causing 
automatic application of any braking system not under 
the control of the anti-lock braking system. 


U-7.4 Trailers with more than 3 axles may utilize the 
T-13 ABS test report provided the following conditions 
are fulfilled: 


U-7.4.1 Irrespective of trailer type at least one third of 
the axles in an axle group shall have all wheels directly 
controlled, with the wheels on the remaining axles 
being indirectly controlled’®. 


0-7.4.2 Utilization of Adhesion: The minimum 
utilization of adhesion specified within M-6.2 is 
deemed to be achieved when following conditions are 
fulfilled: 


U-7.4.2.1 The relationship of the number of wheels 
directly or indirectly controlled by one or more pressure 
modulators and the location of the directly controlled 
wheels within the axle group shall correspond to 
those defined within paragraph 2.2. of the Information 
Document referred to in T-5.2; 


U-7.4.2.2 The utilization of adhesion of the installed 
configuration is shown in the test report as meeting the 
requirements of M-6.2. 


U-7.4.3 Energy Consumption: The number of 
equivalent static brake applications defined within 2.5 
of the test report may be used in conjunction with the 
verification procedure of U-7.3. Alternatively the test 
procedure specified within M-6.1 may be used; 


U-7.4.4 Low speed performance: Additional verification 
is not required; 

U-7.4.5 High speed performance: Additional 
verification is not required; 


U-7.4.6 Category A performance: The split friction 
requirements specified within M-6.3.2 are deemed 
to be fulfilled when the number of wheels which are 
subject to independent left/right control is equal to or 
greater than the number of wheels controlled using 
“select low” axle control; 


U-7.4.7 Surface transition. performance: Additional 
verification not required; 

U-7.4.8 Installation limitations: in all cases the 
following limitations shall apply: 


U-7.4.8.1 Any installation limitations defined within 
2.1 to 2.7 of the information document referred to in 
paragraph T-5.2 shall apply; 


U-7.4.8.2 Only products identified and referenced in the 
information document and test report may be installed; 


U-7.4.8.3 The maximum delivery volume controlled by 
each pressure modulator shall not exceed the volume 
specified within T-14.3.3; 


U-7.4.8.4 An axle with directly controlled wheels 
may only be lifted when any axle which is indirectly 
controlled from this direct controlled axle is lifted in 
parallel; 


16) When the number of axle(s) in an axle group is divided by 3 and the resulting number is less than 1, at least one axle shall be directly 
controlled. When the number of axles in the axle group is divided by 3 and the resulting number is not a whole number, a further axle shall 
be directly controlled in addition to the number of axles indicated by the whole number value. 


156 


U-7.4.8.5 All other installation limitations specified 
within paragraph 4. of the test report shall apply.

U- 9 Functional and installation checks 


U- 9.1 The Certifying agency / Approval authority shall 
carry out functional and installation checks covering 
the following paragraphs: 


U- 9.1.1 Anti-lock Function 


This shall be limited to a dynamic check of the anti- 
lock braking system. To ensure full cycling it may be 
necessary to adjust the load sensing device or utilize a 
surface having a low tyre to road adhesion. If the anti- 
lock system does not have an Annex T approval, the 
trailer shall be tested in accordance with Annex M and 
comply with the relevant requirements contained in 
that Annex. 


IS 11852 : 2019 


U- 9.1.2 Response Time Measurement 

The Certifying agency shall verify that the subject 
trailer conforms to the requirements of Annex E. 

U- 9.1.3 Static Energy Consumption 


The certifying agency shall verify that the subject 
trailer conforms to the requirements of Annex F and 
Annex G as appropriate. 


U- 9.1.4 Service Brake Function 

The Certifying agency shall verify that there are no 
abnormal vibrations during braking. 

U- 9.1.5 Parking Brake Function 

The Certifying agency shall apply and release the park 
brake to ensure correct function. 

U- 9.1.6 Emergency/Automatic Braking Function 

The Certifying agency shall verify that the subject 
trailer complies with the requirements of 5.2.1.18.4.2. 
U- 9.1.7 Vehicle and Component Identification Verifi- 
cation 


The Certifying agency shall check the subject trailer 
against the details contained in the type approval 
certificate. 


U- 9.1.8 Vehicle stability function 


For practical reasons verification of the vehicle stability 
function shall be limited to an installation check as 
defined in U-8.2 and observation of the correct warning 
signal sequence to ensure no faults are present. 


U- 9.1.9 Additional Checks 


The Certifying agency may request additional checks 
to be carried out, if necessary. 


U-10 METHOD OF CALCULATING THE 
CENTRE OF GRAVITY HEIGHT 


The centre of gravity height for the complete vehicle 
(laden and unladen) can be calculated as follows (see 
Fig. 26): 


hl = centre of gravity height of axle(s) assembly 
(inc. tyres, springs, etc)=R. 1.1 

h2 = centre of gravity height of frame (laden) = (h6 
+h8) . 0.5 

h3 = centre of gravity height of payload and 
bodywork (laden) = (h7 . 0.3) + h6 

h4 = centre of gravity height of frame (unladen) = 
h2+s 

h5 = centre of gravity height of bodywork (unladen) 


= (h7 .0.5) +6 +s 


157 


IS 11852 : 2019 


Where, 
h6 — frame height, top 
h7 — body dimensions, inside 
h8 — frame height, bottom 
P — total mass of the trailer 
PR — total mass on all wheels of a semi trailer or centre axle trailer 


R = radius of the tyre 
s = spring deflection between laden and unladen 
ИІ = mass of axle(s) assembly (inc. tyres, springs, etc) = P . 0.1 
W2 = mass of the frame = (P... - W1) . 0.8 
W3 = mass of payload and bodywork 
W4 = mass of bodywork = (P... - WD) . 0.2 


LADEN : UNLADEN: 
— hl.W1+h2.W2+h3.W3 _ hl.W1+h4.W2 + h5.W4 
Rlad Runl 
Ра Punt 


NOTES 
1 For flat bed type trailers, a maximum height of 4 m shall be used. 


2 Fortrailers where the exact centre of gravity height of the payload is not known, it shall be taken as 0.3 times the inside dimensions 
of the body. 


3 For trailers with air suspension, the value of s shall be taken as zero. 


For semi-trailers and centre axle trailers, replace P with PR, wherever it occurs.
